E1.justification: Supplementary Section 3.7(d) and Table 7(a) add FERV39K evaluation, extending coverage to common video FER beyond the retained BioVid, StressID and BAH settings. This is a focused additional benchmark.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables is unchanged. New comparisons reuse EmoCLIP and T3AL; SEV-Net motivates a prompt variant but is not evaluated as an additional baseline model.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce matched window-selection and full-frame controls for T3AL, every-Nth-frame sampling at intervals 2, 3, 5, 10 and 25, and matched training/testing prompt styles. The original subject splits, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Main Table 5 newly isolates window selection and AU tuning. Supplementary Section 3.7 adds matched-window/full-video comparisons, sampling-rate sensitivity and phrase-versus-sentence prompt ablations. Main Figure 5 adds a temporal-selection case study. Together these substantially expand component attribution and robustness analysis beyond v1's retained ablations.

E5.justification: v3 reports StressID performance means and standard deviations over three random seeds for T3AL and CLIP-AUTT in supplementary Figure 5. v1 provides no corresponding seed-based performance uncertainty. This addition is limited to two methods on one dataset; no significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and subject-wise scores remain unchanged, but substantial new findings are reported. FERV39K results include CLIP-AUTT at 51.1 WAR/44.7 F1 versus T3AL at 43.8/38.1. Main Table 5 adds window-only results of 78.7/75.2 and tuning-only results of 80.0/76.4. M1.justification: The frozen CLIP encoders, AU adapter, temporal module, classifier, entropy-guided window selection and AU-embedding adaptation remain unchanged. Sentence-level prompts are tested as an ablation, rather than adopted as a revised method.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language and front-matter edits, adds acknowledgments, and replaces the appendix's qualitative-discussion subsection with Additional Analysis of CLIP-AUTT. The main section sequence and most existing explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The results displays are substantially reorganized and expanded. v1's mixed Figure 4 is separated into qualitative Figure 4 and Table 4, with the fuller appendix qualitative panel moved into the main text. New displays include the temporal-window example, component table, uncertainty/control panels, sampling plot and FERV39K/prompt comparisons.

R1.justification: Supplementary Section 3.7(e) newly relates sentence-level AU prompts to SEV-Net. Otherwise, research positioning is retained; updates to MUSACO and other references concern publication metadata rather than newly cited research.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, main Equations 1–13 and supplementary entropy-gradient explanation are unchanged when checked visually. No new assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations are introduced.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct controls separating the two adaptation components and testing whether baseline input selection explained the gains. v3's main Table 5 and supplementary Section 3.7 address these important evidential gaps, while three-seed estimates strengthen the stability evidence. FERV39K protocol details remain sparse, limiting that extension's reproducibility, but the added controls substantially strengthen support for the unchanged method.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP-AU/CLIP-AUTT research. Their complete main texts and supplementary materials, including tables, figures and rendered equations, support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds FERV39K evaluation, controlled ablations and repeated-seed performance estimates.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on BioVid, StressID and BAH, including benchmark comparisons, subject-wise results, ablations and qualitative analyses.

results.title: CLIP-AUTT: Test-Time Personalization with Action Unit Prompting for Fine-Grained Video Emotion Recognition

C1.justification: The benchmark, training-free method, and superior-performance contributions remain. V2 explicitly elevates cross-domain generalization without retraining and improvement with advancing foundation models into abstract and conclusion claims. The reported headline relative AP margins change from 84%/37.4% to 53.0%/30.6% alongside revised comparisons.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes geometry cues' usefulness for pixel segmentation from their weaker object-level performance, elaborates interpolation versus extrapolation as an explanation for rendering-based baseline failures, and acknowledges possible disadvantage from adapting MV3DCD. It broadens the claimed hyperparameter robustness, although Figure 19 still shows substantial change-threshold sensitivity. The principal ambiguity and reconstruction limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands baseline reproduction instructions, including CYWS-2D training-pair construction, MV3DCD's 60% region assignment rule, and confidence sources. It newly documents scene-consistent splits, collection effort, and using validation-selected parameters across benchmarks. V1 promises future code release; v2 states a self-contained codebase accompanies the supplement, although that attachment cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluation on PASLCD, previously only discussed as prior work. This extends testing to densely captured indoor and outdoor scenes under similar and different lighting conditions. SceneDiff, RC-3D, ChangeSim, and the existing dynamic-content and robotic scenarios remain.

E2.justification: SceneDiff comparisons add MV3DCD and both pretrained and fine-tuned CYWS-2D. The retained Qwen2.5-VL baseline replaces Grounding SAM localization with SAM3. RC-3D adds CYWS-2D and removes the reported VLM comparison. PASLCD comparisons additionally include SplatPose, CSCDNet, CYWS-2D, and MV3DCD, with baseline scores explicitly sourced from prior work.

E3.justification: V1 evaluates prediction centroids inside ground-truth boxes, tolerates two detections per object, and uses the highest-confidence point for scene matching. V2 introduces pixel IoU and mask-based object AP, one-to-one matching at IoU 0.5, and scene matching through aggregated IoU with mean confidence. It also adds CYWS-2D fine-tuning on 3,125 validation frame pairs and direct-box versus SAM-mask evaluation controls.

E4.justification: V2 expands sensitivity testing from change and merging thresholds to three scoring weights and four thresholds. Sections 8.6–8.7 add checks of whether SAM conversion disadvantages CYWS baselines, while Section 8.4 adds trajectory evidence explaining rendering failures. Existing dynamic-person, repetitive-object, lighting, and geometry stress analyses remain; change-type-aware evaluation is revised and relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. V2's discussion of mask confidence concerns detection ranking, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and ablation results are extensively revised. For SD-V, v1 reports point-based per-view/per-scene AP of 49.6/46.3, whereas v2 reports mask-based obj/im and obj/sc AP of 43.8/22.8; these are not directly comparable scores. Reported RC-3D Both AP50 changes from 68.7 to 65.3 and ChangeSim F1 from 57.6 to 57.0. New PASLCD results report 47.3 mIoU versus MV3DCD's 46.1.

M1.justification: The core geometry, segmentation, scoring, and association pipeline remains. Sections 4.2–4.3 change the region exclusion threshold from 60% to 50%, reduce the region-matching weight from 0.2 to 0.1, and replace accepting any sufficiently similar counterpart with one-to-one greedy matching for change classification.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, experimental discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. The benchmark section is reorganized to introduce metrics before dataset and annotation details, and the appendix structure is revised. Method explanations and terminology are also refined beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column main layout with a single-column design and substantially restructures displays. Table 2 groups methods by output type, and ablations use colored differences from the full method. New displays cover scene diversity, PASLCD, expanded sensitivity tests, trajectories, and training examples; the old point-based evaluation illustration is removed and qualitative comparison panels are revised.

R1.justification: Related work expands coverage of sensor-depth, point-cloud, and TSDF approaches, including POCD and Khronos, and adds SAM3 and SplatPose references. GPT-4 and Grounded SAM references disappear with their associated comparison changes. The central positioning around training-free object-level detection remains, with a more qualified account of rendering-based methods' strengths.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain their mathematical forms apart from equivalent notation and parameter retuning. Neither version adds theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations. The revised AP matching criteria are experimental protocol changes rather than new theoretical results.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical validation: mask and track IoU replace permissive single-point matching, stronger baselines make comparisons more demanding, and PASLCD plus conversion and sensitivity checks address important coverage and fairness concerns. These gains outweigh the removed RC-3D VLM comparison and some overstated robustness language. The improvement comes from better evaluation and supporting evidence, not higher reported scores.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SceneDiff benchmark and method. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, equations, tables, and collection guidelines, support comparison. Revised evaluation protocols limit direct score comparisons, not document comparability.

after.justification: V2 reports original revised benchmark results, PASLCD evaluation, expanded sensitivity analyses, baseline adaptation checks, and the retained robotic demonstration.

before.justification: V1 reports original SceneDiff, RC-3D, and ChangeSim results, component ablations, robustness analyses, and a robotic demonstration.

results.title: SceneDiff: A Benchmark and Method for Multiview Object Change Detection

C1.justification: The central dataset, generation and segmentation-benchmark contributions remain. v2 drops the generator's claimed privacy-preserving, full-distribution-surrogate role and presents UniAIMS more explicitly as an optimized Cellpose baseline. Release wording changes from a planned public subset to publicly available EM3M.

C2.justification: The new Open Problems section qualifies v1's strongly positive account with remaining crowding, boundary, contrast and scale failures, supported by PQ falling from 0.704 at IoU 0.5 to 0.340 at 0.9. v2 also acknowledges physically implausible attribute recombinations, explains the augmented-real FID reference, and introduces interpretations concerning external-benchmark saturation and memory bottlenecks.

D1.justification: v2 adds separate dataset, generator and demo access instructions, source proportions, exact sparse-split counts, an SDXL prompt template, and a codebase mapping in Table 7. It expands implementation disclosures concerning LSJ, CUDA flow computation and baseline-specific settings. The reported Aversa-source contribution changes from approximately 500 to 300 images. Conversely, v1's specific Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-o4-mini annotation-model identifiers are omitted.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates segmentation within UniEM-3M. v2 adds zero-shot and fine-tuned evaluation on EMPS and the Okunev dataset, previously discussed only as prior datasets, substantially extending coverage to external transfer evaluation (Table 5). The central collection retains 5,091 images and 2,985,660 masks.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark expands from v1 Table 2 to v2 Table 3 by adding YOLO11-seg, SOLOv2, FastInst, MaskDINO and HoverNet. These are evaluated comparators, not merely new citations. v2's Cellpose comparator cites the same Cellpose-SAM work used in v1; its changed backbone and implementation should not be mistaken for an entirely new comparator.

E3.justification: Dense-subset reporting becomes full-dataset reporting for bottom-up methods. Baseline budgets change from 72 epochs to specified 60,000/180,000-iteration schedules, with revised learning-rate policies. Cellpose changes from ViT-Large to ViT-Base and is documented at 256×256 input resolution. v2 retains default detection limits rather than v1's increased limits. New protocols include the 300-image annotation audit, external transfer evaluation and PQ@90. These are reported protocol revisions, without independently establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative annotation-pipeline validation (Table 2), performance breakdowns by material, morphology and object size (Figure 8), acquisition-hardware analyses (Figure 10), and memory scaling with instance limits (Figure 12). Section 6 additionally tests stricter boundary agreement through PQ@90. The data-volume and synthetic-pretraining analyses already existed in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces statistical annotation-reliability reporting using Krippendorff's alpha from three independent annotators, plus boxplots of memory measurements collected over 1,000 training iterations. Neither version reports repeated-training seed counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for segmentation performance; these additions do not establish repeated independent training runs.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores are extensively replaced under revised settings, preventing direct same-setting performance comparisons. In the data-volume tables, the 30K-synthetic mAP/PQ row changes from 0.773/0.670 to 0.791/0.690, and mixed training changes from 0.807/0.705 to 0.809/0.707; real-data rows remain unchanged. v2 adds annotation, transfer and robustness results. The reported SEM share changes from 90.9% to 84.9%, while FID and Style scores remain identical.

M1.justification: Both versions use a Cellpose-inspired flow predictor with foreground probabilities and a SAM-pretrained ViT-Base backbone, alongside SDXL adaptation using LoRA and learned tokens. v2 newly explains size-model removal, LSJ augmentation and CUDA flow computation as adaptations of Cellpose; it does not establish that these replace a different procedure in v1. Renaming UniEM-Net to UniAIMS is not an algorithmic change.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark discussion and implementation/prediction appendices are extensively rewritten. Dataset construction moves before methodology, the flow explanation expands into dedicated appendix sections, and Open Problems becomes a separate section. Dataset/model terminology, authorship text and citation presentation also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with substantial resizing and relocation of displays. v2 adds annotation, transfer and codebase tables and subgroup, hardware and memory figures. The retained pretraining and t-SNE plots are merged into Figure 6; prediction grids are revised, generated examples expanded, and attribute charts redrawn.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of query-based segmentation, adds OmniScience and privacy/data-sharing literature, and explicitly positions UniAIMS as an implementation adaptation of Cellpose. The underlying materials-dataset gap and principal research lineage remain, making this a bounded expansion and refinement of positioning.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theorems, proofs or substantive formal derivations. v2 Appendix 8 expands the explanation of existing Cellpose flows, scale normalization and reconstruction. The AP formula is retained; distinguishing it from COCO-style AP is clarification rather than a new mathematical definition.

improvement.justification: v1 describes expert annotation review without measuring its reliability; v2 supplies a 300-image independent-annotation audit and stagewise agreement results, addressing an important evidence gap for a dataset paper. Explicit failure conditions, clearer Cellpose attribution and fuller protocol documentation substantially strengthen credibility and interpretation. New reporting flaws temper the gain: the blanket zero-shot superiority claim conflicts with EMPS scores of 0.89 versus 0.92 in Table 5, and the revised 84.9% SEM figure contradicts retained 'over 90%' prose. These flaws do not outweigh the central validation improvements.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dataset, segmentation baseline and diffusion-model project, renamed from UniEM-3M/UniEM-Net to EM3M/UniAIMS. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including tables and rendered figures, and support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation and generation experiments and adds annotation-agreement measurements, external-dataset evaluations and supplementary performance analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation benchmarks, real-versus-synthetic training experiments, generative-model evaluations and dataset analyses, including Tables 2-4.

results.title: EM3M: An Electron Micrograph Dataset for Microstructural Segmentation and Generation

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about grounded instance-level discovery, the GESD benchmark, detection improvement and segmentation applicability. The added dataset-availability statement does not redefine the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The supplement adds interpretations of limited sensitivity to LLM choice, the VLM efficiency tradeoff, and numerical-output instability versus categorical quantization. Section S3.3 also identifies the surfboard-on-land segmentation failure. The main discussion of dataset coverage and incomplete hypothesis spaces remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 supplies generation, matching and evaluation prompts; the HiBug attribute corpus; checkpoint provenance; repair hyperparameters and loss implementation; and A100/vLLM execution details. It also adds a public-availability statement and repository address for GESD. These substantially improve reproducibility information without establishing changes to existing implementations.

E1.justification: Both versions cover GESD detection and segmentation, constructed from COCO, KITTI and face-detection data, plus Waterbirds, CelebA and NICO++. The supplementary results concern these existing tasks and datasets, without establishing additional coverage.

E2.justification: Section S3.1 adds reported component comparisons using GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet for hypothesis generation, and SigLIP and GPT-4o alongside Qwen2.5-VL-7B for matching. The main slice-discovery and repair comparator sets in Tables 1–4 are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added matching-score experiment evaluates alternative score constructions using mAP on a benchmark subset, while Table S1 reports matching speed per 1,000 images alongside Precision@10. These augment the reported evaluation design; the original benchmark and repair settings are not reported as revised.

E4.justification: Section S3.1 supplies substantive additional analyses of LLM choice, VLM precision–speed tradeoffs and matching-score construction. The latter compares yes/no logits, numerical outputs and categorical responses, reporting mAP of 0.47, 0.23 and 0.18. These substantially extend the available component evidence beyond the retained Section 5.2 ablations.

E5.justification: Section S3.1 newly reports five runs for the matching-score ablation. Section S3.5 clarifies randomized seeds and standard-deviation reporting for classification repair. The existing three-repetition detection repair and ten-run classification repair reports remain unchanged; no increase in their run counts is established.

E6.justification: Tables S3–S4 add individual results for 21 detection and 21 segmentation slices, including segmentation average Precision@10 of 0.805 and one zero-scoring slice. Section S3.1 and Table S1 add model, speed and scoring-ablation results. Main Tables 1–4 are unchanged; detection Precision@10 of 0.729 is equivalent rounding of the retained 0.73, not a performance improvement.

M1.justification: The grounded hypothesis construction, VLM matching, monotonic verification and model-repair procedures remain unchanged. The supplement documents previously referenced prompts, implementation choices and the interactive tool; it does not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

P1.justification: The existing main-paper wording and section order are essentially retained. v4 adds an availability sentence and organizes supporting material into supplementary Sections S1–S4, without extensively rewriting or reorganizing the main narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures S1–S14 and Tables S1–S4: prompt panels, dataset-distribution plots, detailed result and attribute tables, and interactive-tool screenshots. This substantially expands the visual documentation. Existing main figures and tables retain their content, with only limited early-page reflow.

R1.justification: The supplement adds the PagedAttention/vLLM serving reference. Its LADDER and FACTS references repeat works already cited in v3. The main related-work discussion, novelty positioning and reference list are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section S3.5 newly formalizes the repair group attribute, weighted detection-head and total losses, and exponential group-weight updates, where v3 describes the weighting verbally. The core matching and trend definitions remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: v3 repeatedly references supplementary prompts, implementation details and segmentation results that its supplied PDF does not contain. v4 resolves this important documentation gap, making the method substantially more reproducible and its segmentation evidence directly assessable. Additional component analyses and dataset-access information strengthen the paper while its main results and scientific claims remain stable.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GH-ESD and GESD, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. v4 retains the main article and adds supplementary Sections S1–S4, which are referenced but absent from the supplied v3.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and supplies additional empirical results, including per-slice segmentation scores and model-selection and matching-score comparisons.

before.justification: v3 reports original slice-discovery experiments, component ablations and model-repair outcomes in Section 5, including Tables 1–4.

results.title: GH-ESD: Grounded Hypothesis-Driven Error Slice Discovery for Instance-Level Vision Tasks

C1.justification: The introduction's empirical contribution now explicitly includes medical imaging, and the conclusion extends demonstrated compatibility to BarlowTwins and BYOL. The abstract and central claims about a target-label-free plug-in regularizer and clustering-based pseudo-counterfactual pairs remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets sensitive-probe reductions as reduced retained sensitive information and large fairness weights as overconstraining representations. The cluster-quality limitation remains, but v1's explicit qualification about setting-dependent warmup and training-schedule tuning is replaced by a shorter warmup-mitigation statement.

D1.justification: v2 supplies settings for the new BarlowTwins/BYOL experiments: 10 clusters, 100 warmup epochs, 5–15 additional fairness-training epochs, and method-specific weights of 0.2 or 0.3. It also describes the frozen-feature sensitive probe. Shared implementation details are unchanged; no ProtoFair code-access or hardware information is added.

E1.justification: v2 adds NIH Chest X-rays for pneumothorax prediction with patient sex as the sensitive attribute, substantially extending evaluation beyond facial images into medical imaging. Existing CelebA attribute tasks and UTKFace imbalance scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: New Table 3 evaluates standalone BarlowTwins and BYOL against their ProtoFair variants, extending comparisons to two noncontrastive SSL objectives. BYOL appeared only as future work in v1. Comparator membership in the original CelebA and UTKFace comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include controlled sweeps over K={3,5,10,15} and lambda={0,0.1,0.3,0.7,1}, frozen-feature sensitive-attribute linear probing, and medical evaluation using AUROC and sex-group AUROC gap. The original CelebA and UTKFace splits, metrics, and reported training schedules are retained.

E4.justification: v1 deferred systematic hyperparameter ablations to future work. v2 adds Section 4.5 and Figure 3 testing cluster-count and fairness-weight sensitivity across four CelebA attribute pairs, plus Table 6 quantitatively testing sensitive-attribute predictability. Existing t-SNE and UTKFace imbalance analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability estimates. The added tables and ablation curves retain point-estimate reporting without uncertainty bars.

E6.justification: All original table values are retained; UTKFace Table 3 becomes Table 4. New Table 3 reports lower EO for all eight BarlowTwins/BYOL task combinations. Table 5 reports SupCon versus SupCon+ProtoFair AUROC of 0.70 versus 0.72 and EO of 1.87 versus 1.79. Table 6 adds reduced sensitive-probe accuracy, and Figure 3 adds sensitivity curves showing accuracy losses at large fairness weights.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same prototype initialization and EMA updates, cross-group positive-pair construction, detached assignments, within-batch and queue losses, and warmup procedure. Applying the regularizer to additional SSL objectives does not introduce a documented algorithmic modification.

P1.justification: v2 tightens wording throughout, condenses the qualitative discussion, adds an ablation subsection, and rewrites future work around autonomous driving and human-robot interaction. The main section order and most methodological and related-work prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Three new result tables (3, 5, and 6) and a four-panel ablation figure substantially expand the visual presentation. Existing tables and surrounding text are repositioned, UTKFace is renumbered Table 4, and captions are shortened. The architecture diagram and t-SNE plots are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Barlow Twins and the NIH chest X-ray dataset and removes the Jigsaw and generative-pretraining references associated with v1's future-work paragraph. BYOL changes from a proposed future evaluation to an evaluated method. Positioning relative to PCL, FSCL, adversarial debiasing, and counterfactual fairness remains stable.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), the positive-set definitions, prototype updates, loss formulations, and cluster-content assumption are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal fairness guarantee is introduced.

improvement.justification: v1 claimed broad plug-in applicability but tested only contrastive base objectives and explicitly deferred sensitivity studies. v2's BarlowTwins/BYOL comparisons and hyperparameter sweeps address these important evidence gaps, while sensitive-attribute probes strengthen the representation analysis beyond t-SNE. The medical experiment adds domain breadth. Sparse medical/probe implementation details, absent uncertainty estimates, and a less specific tuning caveat limit confidence, but the new evidence substantially strengthens support for the central claims.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProtoFair and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references supporting a reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original results for BarlowTwins/BYOL, NIH Chest X-rays, sensitive-attribute prediction, and hyperparameter sensitivity.

before.justification: v1 reports original ProtoFair experiments on CelebA and UTKFace in Tables 1–3 and representation visualizations in Figure 2, alongside baselines attributed to prior work.

results.title: ProtoFair: Fair Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning via Pseudo-Counterfactual Pairs

C1.justification: The central claim of effective detection without real abnormal training videos remains. v2 adds an explicit unseen-class generalization claim in the abstract and introduction and extends its claimed benchmark success to XD-Violence, while retaining the original main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's assertion of a fully fair UVAD comparison with a qualification about additional pretrained generative and vision-language priors. It adds interpretations of detector-space magnitude amplification, abnormal-prototype correction, and usage-aware updates as protection against seen-class overfitting. The existing long-context generation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies detector backbones in Table 4, states that prior-method scores are quoted, and adds XD hyperparameters, guidance settings, and generation costs. The appendix revises the hardware description from one 100 GB GPU to two 96 GB GPUs and updates UCF-Crime's batch size. These are documentation changes; hardware changes or reruns are not independently established.

E1.justification: v2 adds XD-Violence alongside ShanghaiTech and UCF-Crime. It also introduces restricted-class training and evaluation including unseen anomaly classes on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence, substantially broadening the tested scenarios.

XD introduces its 3,954/800 training/test split and 60 pseudo-abnormal plus 50 pseudo-normal clips. The appendix changes UCF-Crime's stated batch size from 4 to 32; whether retained experiments were rerun is unspecified.

E4.justification: v2 adds a randomly selected initial-image baseline, Qwen/C3D feature-norm comparisons in Table 1, and detector-space measurements with domain alignment alone versus full DARM in Table 5b. Tables 8–9 newly test unseen-class robustness. The earlier component ablations and pseudo-clip-count analysis remain.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty. For the new open-set experiments, v2 reports mean AUC and standard deviation over three random class splits. This adds localized variability reporting without establishing additional runs for the retained benchmark results.

E6.justification: New results include XD-Violence AUC of 95.1 with DARM versus 92.5 with UR-DMU, open-set outcomes, an 86.7 SHT random-image baseline, and detector-space norms. Headline SHT/UCF-Crime values remain 98.2/82.5. MGSTRL's SHT score changes from 85.1 to 87.5, overtaking SeeKer; HSC's UCF-Crime and Sultani's SHT entries disappear. Unchanged Table 3 values now have correctly calculated FVD/KVD reductions in the prose.

M1.justification: The CLIP-based image selection, VLM prompt refinement, diffusion generation, and DARM architecture and losses are retained. Scene balancing was already described in v1; v2 clarifies its application without establishing a new algorithmic component or changed detector procedure.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and portions of the introduction and experimental discussion are rewritten; author order and method/appendix headings also change. The overall section sequence and much of the explanatory prose remain, with new scientific content accounting for much of the expansion.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column layout and extensively resizes and relocates material. It merges v1 Figures 4–5 into Figure 4, restructures Tables 1, 4, and 5, adds comparison Tables 7–9, and adds an XD-Violence example to the supplementary video figure.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning SF-VAD/FPL, OpenVAD, DANN, I3D/C3D, and XD-Violence, and removes VideoCrafter2. It also describes Rai et al.'s pretrained-diffusion inpainting more precisely. The broader positioning against UVAD, WVAD, and anomaly-synthesis approaches is retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation is substantively unchanged. v2 numbers the previously inline memory-normalization definition and clarifies negative-prompt notation, but adds no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the proposed mechanism and generalization. Detector-space controls in Table 5b directly investigate the magnitude correction previously supported mainly by accuracy ablations and frozen-feature statistics. Open-set experiments with split variability address previously untested category transfer, while the supervision caveat improves interpretive accuracy. Some main baselines are removed, and attributing open-set gains specifically to DARM remains unablated, but the new evidence provides a substantial overall improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PA-VAD with the same CA-PAG and DARM components. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and document template.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds XD-Violence evaluation, detector-space feature measurements, and open-set experiments with variability across class splits.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation-quality measurements, anomaly-detection results on ShanghaiTech and UCF-Crime, component ablations, and synthesized-data sensitivity experiments.

results.title: PA-VAD: Diffusion-Based Pseudo-Only Video Anomaly Detection via Domain-Aligned Memory Updates

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free zero-shot anomaly generation through delta-denoising attribution, precise masks, realistic localized edits and useful downstream detection data. The expanded experiments do not redefine these principal contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D substantially expands the brief original evaluation caveat into discussions of real-anomaly-dependent diversity metrics, detector and training confounds, benchmark specificity and mask–image alignment. V2 also interprets SAM-free failures as background-placement errors, explains the thresholds' different effects and argues for backbone generality from FLUX results. The original limitations concerning controllability and logical defects remain.
