Training budgets and input processing change, GPT-5 replaces the earlier ChatGPT cleaning description, and explicit training-data-matched comparisons are no longer provided.

E4.justification: v3 adds filtering, curriculum, stain-processing and resolution ablations, plus qualitative retrieval cases. Fusion analysis covers additional query types but removes question-only controls. The modality-gap study changes from t-SNE on Arch datasets against PathCLIP to UMAP on Educontent against several baselines. v2's sample-size robustness analysis is absent from the supplied v3.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. v3's bootstrap procedure filters training data; it does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. v2 Table 4 reports MLLM4PUE-Q R@5 of 47.5%/67.5% on Quilt-VQA/RED; v3 Table 2 reports HOMIE at 67.1%/87.7%. These involve changed models, training and answer processing, not controlled same-setting gains. Newly reported results include 78.5% multi-image-to-text and 30.7% video-to-text R@1.

M1.justification: HOMIE substantially revises MLLM4PUE: LLaVA-NeXT-8B with fixed-resolution inputs becomes Qwen2.5-VL-7B with native-resolution processing. v3 adds text-only retrieval adaptation, subsequent pathology tuning, a morphology-to-diagnosis curriculum, bootstrap filtering and stain normalization/augmentation. These change the procedure beyond renaming or expanded explanation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten around HOMIE/PCR. Results move into the experiments section, composed retrieval becomes the leading evaluation, and the separate zero-shot-transfer explanation is replaced by architecture, adaptation and training-objective sections. This exceeds terminology or numbering changes.

P2.justification: v3 adds a clinical-retrieval workflow to Figure 1, redraws the architecture overview, introduces qualitative examples and replaces the modality-gap plots. Results tables are reordered and substantially restructured; the sample-size chart disappears and component-ablation displays are added. Figure 4 also introduces a caption/legend disagreement over image/text colors.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to MUSK, Pathgen/Patho-CLIP, VLM2Vec, LamRA and GME, positioning HOMIE against both pathology encoders and general multimodal retrievers. The introduction replaces much of the broad diagnostic-task motivation with literature on retrieval, interpretability, hallucination and clinician decision support.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 1 explicitly sums image-to-text and text-to-image contrastive terms. v3 Section 3.4 instead displays a batch-averaged query-to-candidate objective without a reverse term. Section 3.1 also formalizes the broader PCR input/candidate definition, including videos and interleaved inputs. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical support for composed retrieval through distinct multi-image/video tests, more competitive baselines and component controls (Tables 2–6), addressing v2's narrow composed-query validation. The gain is tempered by losing training-data-matched comparisons, incomplete reproducibility details and overstated interpretations: the stain ablation changes composed R@1 only from 53.2 to 53.1, and CONCH overlap is unverified. Nevertheless, the stronger testing of capabilities and design choices constitutes a substantial overall improvement.

A1.justification: These are identifiable versions of the same pathology-embedding work despite extensive revision and renaming. All supplied pages, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Neither PDF contains appendices; both reference separate supplementary material that is unavailable here.

after.justification: v3 Tables 2–6 and Figures 3–4 report original composed retrieval, simple retrieval, classification, qualitative and component-ablation results.

before.justification: v2 Tables 2–5 and Figures 4–5 report original retrieval, classification, embedding-alignment and ablation results.

results.title: Histopathology Multi-modal Embedding for Pathology Composed Retrieval

C1.justification: V2 broadens the abstract and introduction from state-of-the-art performance on VDC with one backbone to two benchmarks, cross-backbone generalization and human-validated preference quality. It also foregrounds faithfulness beyond caption length. Autonomous data generation, curriculum DPO and efficient internalization were already core contributions in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning scorer validity, length and position bias, grounding beyond VDCscore, premature exposure to difficult pairs, and directed reflection versus extra sampling. Some conclusions exceed the evidence: position-bias robustness is asserted despite GPT preference rates changing from 84.4% to 95.2% across input orders.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies 32 sampled frames, 128 tokens per frame, beam size 1, temperature 0.1 and maximum caption length 1024, and supplies a project-page pointer. These are disclosures, not established changes to existing experiments. Most training settings remain unchanged; promised appendix prompts and pseudocode are unavailable.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from VDC alone to include DREAM-1K, comprising 1,000 annotated clips with diverse complexities. This adds substantial independent video coverage. Cockatiel-4K training videos, the five caption dimensions and VDC-Agent-19K remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3-VL-8B and InternVL2.5-8B comparisons. DREAM-1K additionally includes Tarsier-7B and LLaVA-Video-7B. New controls include Best-of-N and anti-curriculum DPO. LLaVA-OneVision's existing VDC baseline is relocated, while vanilla DPO is renamed Random DPO.

E3.justification: V2 adds DREAM-1K event-level precision, recall and F1 evaluation; applies the framework to two additional backbones; and evaluates 500 randomly sampled preference pairs using three blind human raters and GPT-5.1 in both input orders. It also introduces inference-budget comparisons. Dataset-construction totals now refer to eight A800 GPUs rather than one.

E4.justification: New analyses examine preference validity, caption-length bias, evaluator position bias, reversed curriculum ordering and reflection versus Best-of-N under comparable time budgets. Principle robustness adds Shutterstock-derived P4, and principle/iteration studies extend to DREAM-1K. The original greenhouse qualitative example is retained, not newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. V2's separate human judgments and averaging across GPT input orders describe its evaluation protocol, without introducing uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results, including 37.4 F1 on DREAM-1K and human preference rates of 67.6–75.8%, while retaining Qwen's VDC 49.08/2.50. Existing values also change: OwlCap's camera result becomes 46.90/2.50 from 41.30/2.20; Baseline+P2 becomes 45.43/2.30 from 45.83/2.32, and Baseline+P2+R becomes 46.15/2.34 from 46.55/2.36.

M1.justification: The generation, scoring, reflection, preference construction and curriculum DPO pipeline is retained. Equation (3) newly includes video x in both refinement calls, but the PDFs do not establish whether this changes the procedure or clarifies previously implicit inputs. The referenced pseudocode is absent.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction passages and results narrative are rewritten; the agent-related-work discussion, qualitative discussion and conclusion are condensed. Author and affiliation information changes, and acknowledgements are added. These are extensive prose revisions despite retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting. Figure 1 is rearranged, Figure 2 is substantially redrawn, and a caption-length histogram is added. Tables gain backbone blocks, controls and DREAM-1K columns, alongside new comparison tables. The qualitative figure is relocated and reduced; several dense displays become noticeably smaller.

R1.justification: The cited literature expands substantially, including Constitutional AI, Self-Refine, PromptAgent, self-rewarding models, curriculum learning and new benchmark/model references. Several earlier captioning citations disappear. Sections 2–3 gain broader connections to self-feedback and adaptation research, while retaining the central positioning against dependence on external teachers.

T1.justification: Equation (3) adds video x to the refinement/reflection arguments, but it is unclear whether this revises the mathematical definition or makes implicit conditioning explicit. The remaining definitions, DPO loss and curriculum objective are substantively unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's limited validation: another benchmark and two additional backbones test generalization, human judgments assess the self-generated preferences, and new controls probe curriculum ordering and extra-compute explanations. These address important evidential gaps. Missing appendix details, smaller displays and overstrong bias conclusions remain weaknesses, but the broader and more targeted validation provides a substantial net quality improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VDC-Agent work, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. Neither contains appendix pages. V2 repeatedly refers to an absent appendix for prompts, pseudocode, generation analyses and overhead details, limiting comparison of those materials.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds DREAM-1K results, additional backbones, human preference evaluation and further controlled comparisons.

before.justification: V1 reports original VDC benchmark results, component and training ablations, principle and iteration sensitivity experiments, and a qualitative comparison.

results.title: VDC-Agent: When Video Detailed Captioners Evolve Themselves via Agentic Self-Reflection

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same two spectral properties, lightweight LCR/LMR regularizers, backbone independence, 3× convergence speedup, and 10% reward improvement. Reordering the spectral discussion and adding supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation of reconstruction tradeoffs, arguing that latent smoothness need not remove RGB detail and attributing LMR's fidelity cost to precision versus robustness. It discusses capacity/training explanations for the Wan reconstruction gap, distinguishes LCR's structural-affinity effects from LMR's spectral role, and interprets residual-mode diagnostics. It also acknowledges mixed 256p FVD and qualifies applicability under epsilon-prediction.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents batch-level LCR and application of L1, LPIPS, and GAN losses to masked reconstructions. It adds VAE parameter counts, per-step timing measurements, and supplementary-video folder references. These improve technical disclosure, although detailed human-study and timing configurations remain sparse; the code link is unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds DAVIS reconstruction evaluation and downstream image-to-video generation with first-frame conditioning. Appendix A.4 also trains diffusion models on COYO, LAION, and Panda70M; these public datasets previously supported VAE training, while diffusion training used private film/TV clips. These additions broaden task and training-data coverage.

E2.justification: The main generation comparator set and the SER, VA-VAE, and CPR comparisons are retained. v2 Tables 5–6 add a retrained Wan 2.2 VAE as a reconstruction control, extending the evaluated comparison variants.

E3.justification: Beyond revising the 512p regularization schedule, v2 introduces a 1,200-pair human-preference evaluation, public-data diffusion training for 100k steps at 512p, image-to-video first-frame PSNR, and DINO-affinity and corruption-residual diagnostics. These substantially expand evaluation procedures. The revised training description does not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled reconstruction ablations, DINO structural-affinity analysis, CPR/LMR corruption-residual analysis, and measured regularizer overhead. It extends incremental component analysis to VBench and adds generation-quality measurements to the existing LCR hyperparameter study. These provide substantial new tests of fidelity, mechanisms, and efficiency.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new user-study pair count describes evaluation size rather than repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the 512p Baseline FVD from 770 to 970 on VBench and 581 to 681 on MovieGenBench, reversing its displayed ordering against SSVAE. Reconstruction PSNR/LPIPS change from 37.51/0.0339 to 37.84/0.0325 alongside revised finetuning. The LMR-study baseline changes from UR 39.0/FVD 472 to 39.2/471. v2 also adds a 55.7% human win rate and extensive new results; its Figure 2(b) replaces v1's diffusion-loss curves with FVD curves.

M1.justification: The architecture and core LCR/LMR components remain. However, the reported final training stage changes: v1 specifies 2×2×2 masking with revised probabilities during 512p decoder finetuning, whereas v2 Section 5.2 explicitly disables both regularizers. This is a limited revision to the stated training procedure.

P1.justification: v2 places channel eigenspectrum shaping before frequency shaping and revises the abstract and introduction accordingly. It moves the CPR comparison into the LMR discussion, reorganizes reconstruction analysis within the ablations, and restructures the supplement. These are substantial narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout with extensive figure and table rearrangement. v1 Figures 5 and 7 become v2 Figure 3, while Figures 2 and 3 become Figure 4. New preference and reconstruction panels, expanded ablation tables, and supplementary diagnostic displays substantially change presentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bonnaire et al. on diffusion-training dynamics, Ge et al. on FVD content bias, and Seaweed-7B for training-budget context. It also refines positioning relative to structural representation regularization. The main related-work framework and novelty claims remain.

T1.justification: The principal theorem, its proof, and the LCR autocorrelation derivation are retained. Appendix A.1 adds mathematical reasoning about linear noising with affine prediction targets and explains that epsilon-prediction yields isotropic target-input cross-correlation, limiting this diagnostic's ability to distinguish latent modes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation: human preferences supplement automated rewards, public-data diffusion training addresses dependence on private training data, and controlled reconstruction, DAVIS/I2V, and overhead studies test important fidelity and efficiency concerns left weakly supported in v1. Added mechanism and applicability qualifications improve interpretation. Sparse study details and unexplained baseline FVD revisions remain limitations, but the complementary evidence provides a substantial overall quality gain.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSVAE research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Content can be matched across the substantial reordering and reformatting.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds human-preference results, reconstruction tests, public-data validation, and further diagnostic analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation and reconstruction experiments, spectral analyses, component ablations, and hyperparameter studies.

results.title: Delving into Latent Spectral Biasing of Video VAEs for Superior Diffusability

C1.justification: The central claim of efficient, consistent generation through two-stage history learning remains. v6's conclusion adds explicit leadership in five of eight evaluation dimensions and second place in Scene and Cloth, supported by Table 1. It also emphasizes modular compatibility and drops v4's contribution claim of providing pretrained models.

C2.justification: v6 adds substantial interpretations involving frozen-encoder adaptation, LR-branch alignment, consistency versus motion, spatial versus temporal compression, and KV-cache quality costs. It also discusses training-distribution-dependent feature priorities. v4's discussion of apparently reduced drifting in frequently changing shots and its explanation of QwenEdit's object scores disappear.

D1.justification: v6 substantially expands implementation documentation with COLMAP-based retrieval, CLIP sampling at two frames per second, six-neighbor token merging, and external-VAE projection recipes. It newly specifies Stage II LoRA reinitialization, 100k steps for all tabulated ablations, and ELO parameters. Core hardware, encoder channels, and rank-128 LoRA details remain. Referenced full templates and supplementary derivations are unavailable in both supplied PDFs.

E1.justification: The approximately five-million-video training collection and storyboard-generation task remain. However, v6 no longer reports the standalone frame-reconstruction evaluation shown in v4 Table 1 and Figure 5, narrowing evaluation-task coverage while retaining frame-query pretraining. The larger storyboard sample is a protocol change, not a new domain.

E2.justification: v6 Table 1 adds Sliding Window, FOV Retrieval, CLIP Vision, Token Merging, and LTX-VAE+Proj to the generation comparison. FramePack, already evaluated as Large Patchifier for reconstruction in v4, now participates in the consistency comparison. QwenEdit+I2V retains K=1 and K=2 but loses K=3. Several new comparators are explicitly implementations resembling cited methods, rather than evaluations of their complete original systems.

E3.justification: v6 uses Wan 2.1 14B as the default instead of v4's Wan 2.2 configurations, expands 1000 storyboards to 1300, and replaces Gemini-2.5-pro judging with Gemini-3.1-pro and gated Char/Scene/Obj/Cloth scoring. Reconstruction, Aesthetic, and Clarity metrics disappear; CTX/s comparisons are introduced. The batch-capacity example also changes from HunyuanVideo 12.8B to Wan 2.1 1.3B with different windows. These are reported setting changes, not independent proof of reruns.

E4.justification: v6 adds the frozen-encoder ablation testing whether Stage II adaptation is necessary, quantifies previously illustrated extensions, and tests KV-cache compatibility. Its encoding-rate analysis now emphasizes generation consistency. Conversely, v4's reconstruction ablations and quantitative backbone comparison disappear. The pretraining comparison images and existing extension illustrations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v6 adds ELO calculation settings but does not add uncertainty reporting or evidence of increased repetitions.

E6.justification: The quantitative result sets are substantially replaced. v4's reconstruction scores and backbone-specific quality results disappear; v6 adds broad baseline results, a frozen-encoder Char score of 61.42 versus 80.19 for the trainable configuration, and KV-cache FaceID of 63.61 versus 70.71 without caching. These are new comparisons under v6's settings, not demonstrated performance gains or losses between versions.

M1.justification: The dual-branch encoder, randomized frame-query pretraining, joint encoder/DiT finetuning, and incremental history encoding remain. v6 Section 4.6 adds an optional inference procedure that caches history key-value pairs across diffusion steps. Sliding windows, cross-attention, and multiple encoders already appeared in v4.

P1.justification: Beyond the TinyHistory renaming, v6 extensively rewrites the motivation around three history-embedding requirements. It reorganizes the method into architecture, Stage I, Stage II, and inference, and restructures experiments into metrics, baselines, results, ablations, and extensions. This is substantial narrative reorganization, not merely additional results.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout. v6 redraws and combines the training diagrams into a two-stage overview, merges earlier storyboard panels, removes the reconstruction figure, and relocates retained ablation and extension images. Tables are rebuilt around baseline comparisons, ablations, and extensions, with new context-cost columns and metric groupings.

R1.justification: Most related work remains. v6 adds APT, IP-Adapter for Wan Video, and Seedance 2.0, while removing citations including Kling2.5, VBench-2.0, RetinaFace, MUSIQ, SPAQ, and LAION-5B. It expands image-conditioning discussion and sharpens the distinction from frozen compression encoders. Reference renumbering and consolidation of duplicate ToMe entries are presentation changes.

T1.justification: v6 Section 4.2 introduces an explicit custom scoring definition: each qualifying video receives the fraction of three affirmative answers, and dataset scores average only over videos passing the gate. v4 did not specify this rule. Otherwise, the flow-matching objectives remain equivalent; explicit masking and conditional mappings clarify the existing mathematics rather than introduce new theory or proofs.

improvement.justification: v6 substantially addresses v4's narrow evidence for the central generation-quality versus context-cost claim: Table 1 compares seven baseline paradigms on a stated shared backbone, while Tables 2–3 directly test encoder adaptation and quantify extension tradeoffs. The clearer organization also improves assessability. Losing reconstruction and quantitative backbone results reduces supporting coverage, and missing supplements and uncertainty estimates remain limitations, but the stronger evidence for the main contribution outweighs those losses.

A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same two-stage history-encoding work, renamed TinyHistory in v6. Their main texts, equations, tables, and figures are readable. However, neither PDF contains the referenced supplementary material or appendices, limiting verification of appendix-only evaluation templates and implementation details.

after.justification: v6 reports original baseline comparisons, component ablations, extension experiments, and human preference results in Tables 1–3.

before.justification: v4 reports original reconstruction experiments, video-consistency evaluations, backbone comparisons, ablations, and human preference results in Tables 1–3 and associated figures.

results.title: TinyHistory: Lightweight Video History Embeddings via Two-Stage Context Learning

C1.justification: The central claim that specialized signing, fingerspelling, and lipreading experts improve translation through fusion remains. v3 extends the headline state-of-the-art claim to BOBSL and adds provision of generated pseudo-gloss and phoneme annotations for BOBSL and How2Sign as a contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning gating's suppression of irrelevant mouth signals, benefits of diverse pre-training, and the tradeoff between content-word accuracy and function-word reconstruction. Appendix C discusses instructional-domain bias, while Appendix E explains proper-name hallucinations and semantic drift through weak conditioning and LLM priors. v1's discussion was substantially narrower.

D1.justification: v3 adds exact glossing prompts, phonemization tools and fallback handling, parameter counts, fusion architecture dimensions, training schedules, LoRA configuration, hardware, computational costs, and decoding settings. These substantially expand v1's sparse implementation documentation. However, v3 contains conflicting descriptions of epochs, full fine-tuning versus LoRA, and training-time totals.

E1.justification: v3 adds training and evaluation on BOBSL, extending coverage from American Sign Language to British Sign Language and interpreted broadcast footage. YouTube-ASL, How2Sign, and ChicagoFSWildPlus remain in use.

E2.justification: Geo-Sign is newly included in the How2Sign comparison, having only been cited in v1. The new BOBSL comparison includes GFSLT, Sign2GPT, Albanie, Sincan, and Lost in Translation. Appendix B additionally compares concatenation/MLP and cross-attention fusion alternatives and multiple YouTube-ASL baseline configurations. The fingerspelling comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds zero-shot transfer and How2Sign-only training controls, standalone phoneme evaluation, and POS accuracy analysis. It drops BLEU-2/3 from the main benchmark comparison and no longer reports sequence-classification accuracy. Optimization is reported as AdamW rather than v1's Adam; most other newly supplied hyperparameters are disclosures, not established changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds fingerspelling, fusion, and sequencer removal ablations; standalone expert tests; alternative fusion comparisons; pre-training/transfer analysis; POS analysis; and label-length analysis. Qualitative cases are replaced and extended to BOBSL. Conversely, v1's quantitative comparison of random, frequency-based, keyword, and LLM glossing methods is removed rather than relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional v3 results continue to use point estimates.

E6.justification: Reported How2Sign BLEU-1/BLEU-4 changes from 46.0/23.5 to 49.4/22.1, while ROUGE remains 41.2 and fingerspelling accuracy remains 73.2%. The no-lipreading BLEU-4 changes from 16.6 to 13.6. v3 adds BOBSL BLEU-4 of 6.8, zero-shot 8.3, How2Sign-only 13.7, and numerous analytical results. These are revised or newly reported results, not established same-setting performance gains.

M1.justification: The expert-routing, CTC, gated-fusion, and LLM pipeline remains. v3 changes manual inputs from hand crops to full frames and changes the main-text gate from manual-only conditioning to concatenated manual/lip features (v1 Equation 10; v3 Equation 12). It also describes independent decoder training on generated gloss/text pairs instead of v1's final training on fusion outputs.

P1.justification: Beyond the title and model rename, v3 extensively rewrites the introduction and method, reorganizes the pipeline into numbered stages, and develops a structured appendix with a contents list and dedicated analysis and implementation sections. This is substantial narrative restructuring, not merely added experimental content.

P2.justification: v3 adds an opening modality illustration, redraws the architecture diagram, replaces the earlier routing visualizations with different translation displays, and introduces a POS heatmap and label-length plots. Comparison tables are restructured, and new appendix tables document analyses, configurations, and intermediate fused outputs.

R1.justification: v3 adds related-work coverage including SAGE, SLTUNET, hierarchical feature alignment, and Lost in Translation, alongside component references such as DINOv2, Gumbel-Softmax, and LoRA. The underlying positioning remains the absence of explicit fingerspelling/lipreading integration in prior SLT systems; publication and bibliographic updates do not constitute additional scientific changes.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a mathematical complexity comparison between O(T) gating and O(T²) cross-attention operations. Expanded CTC formulas mostly unpack losses already present in v1. Neither version presents a theorem or proof framework.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves important components and fusion choices weakly tested and provides few implementation settings. v3's expanded component tests, direct fusion comparisons, BSL evaluation, transfer analysis, and explicit failure discussion substantially strengthen the evidence and make the method easier to assess. Removal of the glossing-method ablation and inconsistent training disclosures weaken parts of the revision, but do not outweigh these substantial gains in scientific support and transparency.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same three-expert sign-language translation framework, renamed from MultiStream-LLM to SignBind-LLM. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials support a reliable comparison.

after.justification: v3 reports original results on How2Sign, ChicagoFSWildPlus, and BOBSL, together with additional component, fusion, transfer, and linguistic analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original How2Sign translation and ChicagoFSWildPlus fingerspelling results, component ablations, temporal-alignment experiments, and qualitative examples.

results.title: SignBind-LLM: Multi-Stage Modality Fusion for Sign Language Translation

C1.justification: The introduction restricts the claim that training objective outweighs architecture to the evaluated model set and acknowledges that these factors are not fully decoupled. The conclusion similarly replaces 'matters more' with 'a major factor beyond architecture alone.' The central benchmark, object-centricity, and Gram-alignment contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges architecture/objective confounding and adds interpretations addressing readout capacity, global teacher distillation, classification performance, response bias, and condition-specific effects. The conclusion also moderates its characterization of patch correlations as a fundamental organizing principle to an important contributor.

D1.justification: Section 6.2 supplies previously missing feature dimensions, readout architecture, losses, optimizers, learning rates, schedules, epochs, gradient accumulation, and training-only RT normalization. It specifies last-block-only Gram fine-tuning and classification/Gram loss weights of 1/10. The abstract adds a code/data access link; its external availability was not checked.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same COCO2017-based grouping and reaction-time tasks, 72 participants, 255 experimental images, and 1,020 behavioral trials, alongside ImageNet training. The supplementary analyses examine this retained coverage rather than introducing another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: The nine main backbones remain unchanged. Sections 6.2–6.3 add focused comparators: linear RT readouts across all nine models, CLS-token distillation for IN21k and IN1K ViT B, and fine-tuning without Gram loss for the ImageNet-accuracy comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises the stated 10-fold RT protocol to nested validation, adding an inner 90/10 training–validation split for early stopping and hyperparameter selection. Table 1 also changes DINO ViT B's large-dataset designation from Yes to No. These reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun or a different checkpoint was evaluated.

E4.justification: New supplementary analyses examine subject and condition accuracy, sensitivity, response bias, RT-distribution separation, and directional consistency. Linear-readout and CLS-distillation controls test alternative explanations for alignment, while Figure 8 and Table 2 examine correlations within each condition. These substantially expand validation beyond v1's retained layer/head and Gram-alignment analyses.

E5.justification: v2 adds significance reporting for the cross-model association and supplementary analyses, subject-level dispersion statistics, and the noise ceiling's standard deviation of 0.037. The existing 10 seeds per fold and 20 subject splits remain unchanged; no increase in repetitions is established.

E6.justification: Table 1's grouping accuracies and the main plotted results are retained, but substantial supplementary findings are added. These include linear-readout association r=0.917, condition-specific correlations, raw model–human correlations, and behavioral sensitivity/bias results. CLS distillation yields 0.59→0.59 and 0.59→0.58 for the two ViTs, compared with Gram alignment's 0.59→0.72 and 0.59→0.70. These are additional comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

M1.justification: The proposed patch-feature readout, object-centricity analysis, and Gram-alignment procedure are retained. Section 6.2 newly documents architecture and training details without establishing a changed method; linear readout and CLS distillation are additional comparison methods.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. Changes include localized clarification of validation, normalization, ROC definitions, and Gram similarity; qualified claims; supplementary cross-references; keywords and affiliation edits; and a new supplementary section organized into three subsections.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the document with a narrower text area, running headers, resized and repositioned figures, and wrapped Table 1 headings. It adds the four-panel Figure 8 and Tables 2–3, while retaining the main figure content. This is a substantial layout revision beyond pagination changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al.'s 'Unsupervised segmentation in real-world images via Spelke object inference' to the introductory positioning. The related-work narrative otherwise remains substantially unchanged; publication and bibliographic updates to retained references do not represent additional research coverage.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the stated ROC definitions: fractions of active patches falling inside/outside an object become threshold-positive fractions among within-/outside-object patches. This is a mathematical-definition correction; the displayed ROC results and Gram-matrix mathematics are retained, and neither version supplies formal proofs.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited controls and missing reproducibility information. The supplementary readout and distillation comparisons strengthen assessment of the central mechanism, while behavioral checks, raw correlations, and detailed training specifications make the evidence easier to evaluate and reproduce. Corrected ROC definitions and narrower architecture/objective claims improve precision. These gains concern evidential support and transparency, rather than higher headline performance.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, behavioral experiment, models, and main analyses. All pages, figures, tables, and the supplementary material added in v2 are readable; v1 ends with references.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds behavioral analyses, linear-readout and CLS-distillation controls, and condition-specific model–human correlations.

before.justification: v1 reports original results from 72 participants, model predictions of grouping judgments and reaction times, object-centricity analyses, and Gram-alignment experiments.

results.title: Human-like Object Grouping in Self-supervised Vision Transformers

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction elevate particularly strong 4-bit benefits into the headline claims, and the introduction explicitly distinguishes the motivating observations from behavior in smaller ViTs. The central contribution—training-free outlier mitigation through universal middle-layer prefixes and token deletion—remains intact.

C2.justification: v4 substantially extends applicability and deployment interpretations: reconstruction-based selection reduces dependence on labeled validation, interpolation supports dense prediction, and FP16 retention trades accuracy for a computational bottleneck. Section 5.4 adds an interpretation of vision-encoder bottlenecks after LLM acceleration, while Appendix P contrasts SmoothQuant with vision-specific quantization. The original outlier-emergence explanation and stated hyperparameter-tuning limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly specifies PTQ4ViT/ERQ calibration counts and FIMA-Q optimization/calibration budgets, and gives more specific GPU assignments, including A100 80GB hardware. Table 6 documents TensorRT, A6000 hardware and standalone batch size. These improve documentation; newly disclosed budgets do not establish changes to previously conducted experiments.

E1.justification: v4 adds image question answering on GQA and VQAv2, video understanding on Video-MME and MLVU, and semantic segmentation on ADE20K. Classification coverage also expands to Caltech101, Oxford-IIIT Pet and DTD. These introduce substantially different tasks and input conditions beyond the retained classification and retrieval evaluations.

E2.justification: ERQ is newly evaluated in the ImageNet-1k and MS-COCO comparisons, and SmoothQuant becomes an evaluated comparator in Appendix P rather than merely a citation. FIMA-Q, QuaRot and test-time registers were already evaluated in v3; their relocation does not constitute new baselines.

E3.justification: Retrieval evaluation adds W4A4 for the previously W6A6/W8A8-only baselines and removes R@5 reporting; FIMA-Q already had W4A4 results. New VLM and segmentation experiments introduce additional configurations and metrics. v3's whole-validation-set timing and FLOPs evaluation is replaced by TensorRT/A6000 latency measurements, including batch-64 standalone encoders and VLM prefill timing. These timing results are not directly comparable across versions. AWQ evaluation also narrows from four encoders to CLIP.

E4.justification: New analyses test label-free reconstruction-based selection, FP16 retention versus token deletion, sink/random/non-sink segmentation behavior, spatial interpolation, and transfer of SmoothQuant to vision encoders (Appendices H, K, L and P). The original caching/deletion ablation, insertion-layer sensitivity and tokenization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same cosine-similarity means and ± values. Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests; the added result tables continue point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive VLM, segmentation, ERQ, SmoothQuant and variant results, while removing R@5, three encoders' AWQ results and the old FLOPs/timing entries. Existing values also change: Table 2's SigLIP2 PTQ4ViT+RegCache W6A6 accuracy changes from 68.17 to 69.02. FIMA-Q classification results are reassigned between CLIP/OpenCLIP, resolving v3 Table 8's inconsistent labels. A new inconsistency appears: v4 Table 2 reports a SigLIP W6A6 best gain of 3.38, although its PTQ4ViT rows imply 3.70.

M1.justification: The core curating, KV-caching and token-deletion procedure remains unchanged. v4 adds bounded variants: reconstruction-MSE selection of prefix/deletion counts, replacement of deleted tokens by spatial interpolation for segmentation, and FP16 token processing instead of deletion (Appendices K, H and L).

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into setup, main results, analyses, latency and other experiments; the appendices are extensively reordered, with some material moved into the main text. These are substantial narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 Figure 1 is reworked into a PTQ-pipeline overview and a separate sink-token schematic. FIMA-Q results are consolidated into enlarged benchmark tables, retrieval tables are redesigned, and new VLM, latency and analysis tables are added. Appendix figures and tables are extensively relocated and repaginated.

R1.justification: v4 expands positioning toward VLM deployment and efficiency through Qwen3-VL, LLaVA, FastVLM and related literature, alongside ERQ and new benchmark references. Related work adds a dedicated outlier-control comparison and clarifies the relationship to training-free, concurrent test-time registers. Several earlier references, including APHQ-ViT, DOPQ-ViT and the robotics/survey motivation, are removed.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 and its proof, including Equations (3)–(6), are mathematically unchanged between v3 Appendix B and v4 Appendix F. The principal method definitions in Equations (1)–(2) also remain unchanged; the new variants do not introduce new formal theoretical results.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important gaps in v3's practical validation: VLM image/video experiments and TensorRT measurements directly support deployment relevance, while segmentation and label-free selection tests address spatial-output and supervision constraints (Tables 4, 6, 11–14). These substantially strengthen evidence for the method's applicability. Removing R@5 and most AWQ results reduces retained evidence, and the new Table 2 summary inconsistency weakens reporting accuracy, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the gains in validation of central claims.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RegCache research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v4.

after.justification: v4 reports original vision-encoder experiments and adds VLM, segmentation, latency and method-variant results, including Tables 4, 6 and 11–15.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification and retrieval experiments, outlier measurements, ablations and computational-efficiency results in the main text and appendices.

results.title: Activation Quantization of Vision Encoders Needs Prefixing Registers

C1.justification: The central contribution remains efficient, mask-agnostic hierarchical pretraining with ViT-level microscopy segmentation. V2 refines the headline contributions toward reusable segmentation decoding, 2× pretraining and 5× fine-tuning speedups, and better slit segmentation than grid-based hierarchies, replacing v1's emphasis on up to 7× FLOP reduction.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of token-location interpretability, volumetric applicability, and bandwidth/cache limitations that can erode efficiency at very high resolutions. It also replaces v1's interpretation of robustness at 75% masking with an account of noticeable degradation and explains the failure of deepest-stage-only reconstruction.

D1.justification: Supplementary Sections 7.1–7.7 add architecture configurations, cached-neighbor implementation details, preprocessing parameters, segmentation-head adaptation, benchmark-specific optimization settings, and measured pretraining hours. Hardware disclosure also expands to identify H100-trained baselines, although this conflicts with the main text's blanket RTX 5090 description.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluations on Lucchi++, Kasthuri++, and the 2012 ISBI EM Challenge, substantially broadening microscopy coverage beyond FPW. The reported FPW segmentation task also narrows from four foreground classes to the basement-membrane interface and filtration slits, retaining background.

E2.justification: The FPW comparison expands from ViT-MAE in v1 Table 1 to include SimMIM, MixMAE, GreenMIM, HiViT, and nnU-Net V2 in v2 Table 2. These are evaluated comparators, whereas several appeared only as related work in v1.

E3.justification: Reported main models increase from approximately 22M to 65M parameters, with pretraining/fine-tuning schedules changing from 300/700 to 400/400 epochs. FPW test size changes from 164 to 235, and resolutions from 448/512/768 to 512/768/1024. V2 also introduces CLAHE preprocessing, UperNet baseline heads, Slits IoU and FPW-error metrics, revised memory-measurement batch sizes, and public-benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: V2 adds controls for initialization source, deepest-stage-only reconstruction, ViT with the point decoder, and cached versus standard decoder execution. It removes v1's training-data-fraction study (Figure 11) and the 65% masking-ratio ablation entry. Existing representation-collapse and spectral analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Table 2 first reports main FPW scores as mean ± standard deviation across four random seeds. Table 4 additionally reports timing variation over 30 trials. V1 provides point estimates without corresponding model-run or uncertainty information; an increase from a known v1 run count cannot be established.

E6.justification: Main and ablation results are extensively replaced: AFFMAE's 512-pixel mIoU is 0.6030 in v1 Table 1 versus 0.608 ± 0.002 in v2 Table 2 under revised settings, not a same-setting gain. V2 adds FPW errors, decoder timings, and public-benchmark results, including AFFMAE mIoUs of 0.8829, 0.8870, and 0.8661 in Table 6.

M1.justification: V2 introduces cached, quantized-grid KNN retrieval in place of separate neighbor searches for decoder queries (Sections 3.3 and 7.1). This is a localized procedural change to the retained framework of adaptive merging, stable interpolation, Perlin masking, and deep supervision.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, related work, method explanations, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Method subsections are reorganized, ablations precede main results, and dedicated discussion/limitations and supplementary sections replace the earlier compact structure.

P2.justification: V2 switches to a single-column layout, merges existing collapse and masking figures, redesigns efficiency displays, and substantially expands comparison-table structure. New architecture/cache diagrams and qualitative panels are added, while v1's data-efficiency plot is removed. These are substantive display changes beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

R1.justification: Research positioning substantially shifts toward kidney ultrastructure and comparisons with sparse hierarchical masked-modeling approaches. V2 adds GreenMIM, HiViT, clinical FPW, public-benchmark, and segmentation-decoder references while removing the separate adaptive-token survey covering DynamicViT, A-ViT, and AdaViT. The earlier broad criticism of competing hierarchical methods is rewritten.

T1.justification: V2 adds limited complexity arguments: cached KNN retrieval is effectively O(1) per query after table construction, and the volumetric discussion derives O(n^6) versus O(n^4) dense-attention scaling. Core interpolation and normalized-effective-rank mathematics remain equivalent; no theorem or proof framework is introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially remedies v1's narrow validation through additional FPW baselines, three public EM benchmarks, four-seed reporting, and fuller implementation and limitation disclosures. These strengthen evidential breadth and reproducibility. The removed low-data study, inconsistent GPU descriptions, and SimMIM prose/table discrepancy are drawbacks; revised FPW settings also prevent direct version-to-version performance claims. They do not outweigh the stronger support for the central accuracy-efficiency contribution.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AFFMAE and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Inspection includes v2's supplementary Section 7; v1 ends after its references. The substantial revisions can be matched reliably.

after.justification: V2 reports original FPW comparisons, component and decoder experiments, and evaluations on three public electron-microscopy benchmarks.

before.justification: V1 reports original FPW segmentation, computational-efficiency measurements, component ablations, and training-data-efficiency experiments.

results.title: AFFMAE: Scalable Vision Pre-Training for High-Resolution Microscopy Segmentation on Desktop Hardware

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the central theoretical contribution from a claimed proof of signal/noise decomposition to approximate separation under a multiplicative assumption. The abstract also replaces the headline 'up to 75%' improvement with a seven-benchmark claim focused on visual perception and recent as well as earlier models. CARVE's training-free contribution and attention-complexity observations remain.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains gains in terms of perceptual task demands, scale normalization, and model capability. Its main-text limitations and Appendix J identify loss of global spatial context, demonstrate a depth-ordering failure, acknowledge nonlinear attention interactions and imperfect uniformity, and discuss the accuracy–inference-cost tradeoff. These materially qualify applicability beyond v1's discussion of excessive masking.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-code link, specifies lambda=0.05, documents extended dataset splits and sample counts, attention-fusion settings, mask parameters, scoring procedures, and resource-measurement conditions. Hardware reporting expands from four RTX A6000 GPUs to an A6000/H20 allocation. These are substantial documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish that newly disclosed settings changed existing experiments or verify the linked code's availability.

E1.justification: v3 retains A-OKVQA, POPE, V*, and TextVQA and adds evaluated document understanding, chart comprehension, and science-question reasoning through DocVQA, ChartQA, and ScienceQA (Table 3). Appendix J additionally examines a BLINK relative-depth failure case; this is a single case, not a full BLINK benchmark evaluation.

E2.justification: SD-RPN is newly evaluated alongside ViCrop and CARVE in v3 Table 3, adding a trained region-selection comparator. The existing SAM, YOLO, CLIP, and three ViCrop variants remain in the corresponding TextVQA comparison, moved from v1 Table 3 to v3 Table 5. The comparator membership change is limited.

E3.justification: New protocols include sampled DocVQA validation data, ChartQA and image-containing ScienceQA test sets, EM/ANLS/relaxed/multiple-choice metrics, component controls, temperature variation, and resource measurements over 100 ChartQA samples. Appendix I adds Qwen3-VL-2B/4B and Gemma-3-27B-it configurations. The retained external-tool timing comparison is relabeled from GPU time to end-to-end inference latency with unchanged values; this is a reported metric revision, not evidence that those measurements were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds controls testing direct question-attention masking and internal attention modification (Table 4), multiplicative versus additive contrast and attention uniformity (Appendix G), decoding-temperature robustness (Appendix B.3), measured inference overhead, and a BLINK depth-reasoning failure analysis. These substantially expand investigation of mechanism, robustness, and failure conditions beyond v1's retained time-step, layer, masking, and prompt studies.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix H adds V* bootstrap confidence intervals using 10,000 resamples and paired McNemar tests for all four original models. Table 11 adds means and standard deviations for attention-uniformity measurements over 500 images, and Appendix B.1 specifies a DocVQA sampling seed. The existing Figure 5 confidence intervals and ten-trial prompt study remain; their presence is not new.

E6.justification: Substantial new benchmark, ablation, newer-model, timing, memory, and failure-case results are reported. Existing values also change: Table 1's LLaVA-1.5-13B Tfull scores move from 76.5 to 76.9 on A-OKVQA and 70.0 to 70.2 on V*. Table 2 changes Qwen2.5-VL-3B's [20,25] V* score from 57.1 to 56.5 and LLaVA-1.5-7B's corresponding TextVQA score from 58.2 to 57.9. These are reported numerical revisions, not established performance gains from a changed method.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same general/task-specific attention extraction, regularized attention ratio, weighted fusion, top-p thresholding, top-K connected-region selection, masking, cropping, resizing, and final inference. Additive contrast and internal attention modification are experimental alternatives, not revisions to CARVE. Appendix I explicitly applies the unchanged pipeline to newer models.

P1.justification: v3 extensively condenses and rewrites retained introduction, related-work, attention-analysis, and results passages. Section 3 and its subsections receive clearer descriptive titles, 'Method Analysis' becomes 'Experiments,' and implementation, validation, statistics, and limitations receive expanded organization. This exceeds the structural changes attributable solely to added experiments.

P2.justification: The paper adopts substantially different typography, margins, headers, float placement, and table styling. Existing results tables replace green highlighting and parenthesized gains with bold/underlined rankings and superscript gains. Numerous new tables and two new case-study figures are added. The original prompt table and masking visualizations are retained and renumbered, not replaced.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused toward visual-token processing, attention-head methods, and trained grounding/zooming systems, adding discussion of CogCoM, CogAgent, Ferret-UI, and visual-explanation methods. v3 explicitly credits ViCrop as inspiration and introduces SD-RPN positioning. Earlier discussion and references concerning RECIPE, DistiLLM-2, BLIP-2, and other works are removed; retained works' publication updates are not counted as new research.

T1.justification: The decomposition becomes an explicit modeling assumption, and Appendix C qualifies uniqueness and the retained results as properties of an idealized model. v1's approximation-error bound, optimal-regularization proposition, and entropy-monotonicity theorem in C.4–C.6 are removed. Convexity and closed-form derivations remain. The computational analysis is retained with corrected numerical examples, including combined speedup changing from 1.24 to 1.19.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important evidential gap: new component and additive-contrast controls directly test CARVE's central design choices, while V* significance analyses support the large gains on a small benchmark. Broader evaluations, measured overhead, and a concrete failure case improve assessment of applicability and practical cost. Explicit theoretical assumptions and removal of overstated results also improve claim calibration. The decomposition remains an idealized model, but the paper now provides substantially stronger empirical support and clearer boundaries.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CARVE research, with matching authors, title, algorithm, and original experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, component ablations, statistical analyses, resource measurements, newer-model experiments, and a failure case.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention analyses, CARVE evaluations on four benchmarks, comparisons with other methods, and hyperparameter and prompt experiments.

results.title: Focusing by Contrastive Attention: Enhancing VLMs' Visual Reasoning

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: GR-IQA, interactive region-aware Zoom-IQA, KL-Coverage and resampling, and claims of reliable reasoning, generalization, and downstream usefulness. Added evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: New discussions interpret learned cropping versus fixed cropping, semantic grounding of selected regions, and RL versus supervised imitation. The supplement additionally addresses evaluator self-preference, artistic bokeh versus defects, background noise, and deployment latency. These introduce substantive mechanism explanations and applicability arguments absent from v1.

D1.justification: v3 adds timing hardware/software information (NVIDIA H200 NVL and vLLM) and revises SFT accumulation steps. It removes the disclosed score-reward sigma of 0.35, detailed GRPO/token-masking specification, and identification of SwinIR in restoration preprocessing. Prompt templates, filtering thresholds, reward weights, and the project link remain.

E1.justification: The seven IQA datasets and existing restoration tasks remain. v3 adds quantitative restoration coverage on synthetic DIV2K and real-world RealLQ250, plus targeted background-bokeh and night-noise examples, including FoundIR. DreamClear itself was already evaluated in v1's supplement.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged, including DeQA renamed DeQA-Score. v3 adds Qwen2.5-VL-7b as a saliency-grounding comparator in Table 6 and central-crop and separately defined single-stage SFT controls in Table 5.

E3.justification: New protocols include quantitative restoration metrics, QAGNet-based crop evaluation using area/SDL/F0.5, Grok-4-1-fast judging, a human-ranking study with 15 annotators on 30 images, and runtime testing. Section 4.1 also changes reported SFT gradient accumulation from eight steps to four; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained component ablations, v3 adds crop-policy and training-paradigm controls, saliency-grounding analysis, independent judge/human checks addressing evaluator self-preference, and background-bokeh/night-noise case studies (Tables 5-7; Figures 14-15). These substantially expand tests of the central mechanism and evaluation validity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed variation, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added human-study sample counts concern evaluation design. The retained Confidence rubric measures assertiveness of language, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-2 and the original component ablation table remain unchanged after matching layouts. Tables 3 and 5-8 add substantial results, including KonIQ PLCC of 0.938 versus 0.898 for central cropping. Restoration findings are mixed: Zoom-IQA leads several perceptual metrics, but SUPIR PSNR is 21.31 versus Q-Insight's 22.44.

M1.justification: The backbone, VRF/HACF filtering, two-stage SFT/GRPO training, crop-and-refine procedure, rewards, KL-Coverage regularizer, and progressive resampling remain. Sample-level HACF wording clarifies v1's existing procedure. The total-reward formula moved from v1 Supplement Section 10.1; it is not a new objective.

P1.justification: v3 revises VRF/HACF explanations, moves existing restoration and total-reward material into the main text, and adds discussion sections, an author, and acknowledgments. Most existing abstract, introduction, results interpretation, and conclusion prose remains, so language and narrative restructuring are limited.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. Existing result tables are reorganized into stacked metric or dataset blocks, figures are resized and relocated, and captions are revised. Five new result tables and Figures 14-15 substantially expand the displays; original supplementary examples are largely retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds brief discussion of VQ-Insight and Reasoning as Representation. Other new citations support saliency, runtime, and restoration evaluation, while DeepSeekMath and SwinIR citations disappear. The central positioning against non-interactive, text-only IQA reasoning remains unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 removes v1 Supplement Section 10.2's explicit masked GRPO objective (Equation 7), probability-ratio definition, and token-validity-mask definition. The other method equations remain, including the relocated total-reward formula. This reduces formal specification without establishing an algorithm change.

improvement.justification: The crop-policy controls, saliency evaluation, and independent Grok/human assessments substantially strengthen validation of the central region-aware reasoning claim beyond v1's component ablations, model judges, and examples. Quantitative restoration results also expose metric-dependent tradeoffs. These gains outweigh the loss of some GRPO and reproducibility details, although the human study is small and statistical uncertainty remains unreported.

A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Zoom-IQA and GR-IQA work. Their main text and complete supplements support reliable comparison, including matching equations, tables, and qualitative examples across substantial reformatting.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative restoration, crop-policy and saliency evaluations, human rankings, another model judge, and runtime measurements.

before.justification: v1 reports original IQA benchmark results, reasoning evaluations, component ablations, and SUPIR/DreamClear restoration examples.

results.title: Zoom-IQA: Image Quality Assessment with Reliable Region-Aware Reasoning

C1.justification: V1 presents CASA as a new fusion mechanism whose local text self-attention and implicit gating are crucial to closing the performance gap. V2 instead centers the claim that vanilla cross-attention is competitive under comparable modern training, with joint text-image attention becoming one variant. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the original novelty claim with a controlled comparison organized around five design differences.

C2.justification: V1's explanation that missing text interaction causes cross-attention's weakness, and that implicit gating remedies it, is withdrawn. V2 emphasizes training comparability and interprets joint text-image attention as offering little average advantage over vanilla CA. It also develops the limitations of losing explicit visual history, the proposed role of delimiter tokens as compressed memory, and the tradeoffs of parameter sharing and layer replacement.

D1.justification: The reproducibility recipe is substantially revised: v2 documents different accumulation settings, training horizons and runtimes, and reports AdamW instead of Adam. It specifies frame-wise video windows, delimiter-based history, absence of positional embeddings in plain CA, and frozen image temporal positions for CAt+v. V1's detailed profiler procedure and explicit caption-training mixture description are removed. The project-page access and code/model-release statements remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The represented dataset and task coverage remains image understanding, video QA, and live captioning, using the same FineVision, LLaVA-OneVision, LLaVA-Video, and Live-Whisper dataset families. The nine image benchmarks, five video benchmarks, and LiveSports3K evaluation are retained. Windowing, resolution, and architectural comparisons change procedures within this coverage.

E2.justification: The external baseline set in Table 2 is retained. However, v2 Figure 1 adds EVLM-Chat 14B and StreamChat to its image comparison, and Table 4 adds StreamChat to video comparisons. The controlled gated/register cross-attention comparisons and the Q-64 qualitative caption comparison from v1 are removed.

E3.justification: Helium training changes from 100k to 40k steps, and Qwen image adaptation from 60k in v1's main text or 65k in its appendix to 25k. Training resolution changes from 896 squared pixels for CASA and 672 squared for insertion to 952 squared for both; video resolution changes from 448 squared to 504 squared. V2 increases insertion gradient accumulation to match token budgets and introduces explicit per-frame versus all-frame video comparisons and revised efficiency measurements.

E4.justification: V1's self-versus-random-token masking experiment, attention-distribution analysis, and detailed layer-placement study are removed or replaced. V2 adds parameter-sharing and revised layer-frequency comparisons, contrasts video-history mechanisms, and expands convergence analysis to individual benchmarks for both backbones. FFN-update and token-compression analyses remain, while the detailed layer-level profiling and Q-64 qualitative case study disappear.

E5.justification: V1 Table 11 explicitly averages profiling measurements across 100 calls. That experiment and its repetition-count disclosure are absent from v2, whose replacement efficiency table gives no equivalent count. Neither version reports seed-based accuracy uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The main image and video result tables contain substantially replaced and added results. For example, the parallel joint-attention Helium model's ChartQA score changes from 73.8 to 75.3 under revised training conditions, so this is not an established same-setting gain. The Q-Former-128 aggregate changes from 62.7 to 63.8 despite unchanged component scores. Conversely, the FFN-update ablation and LiveSports captioning scores are retained.

M1.justification: The original parallel CASA operation survives as CAt+v; that renaming alone is not a method change. However, v2 introduces shared CA/self-attention projections and replacement of self-attention layers with plain CA. Video-QA processing also changes from a whole-video attention window to per-frame windows using image delimiters to retain compressed history, with the all-frame alternative additionally evaluated.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method narrative, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The CASA-centered approach section becomes a five-part comparison of cross-attention and token insertion, terminology changes throughout, and the appendices are reorganized after removing the implicit-gating section.

P2.justification: The opening radar comparison becomes a normalized grouped bar chart, and the architecture/attention illustrations are reorganized into a combined multipanel figure. Efficiency and video tables receive substantially different structures; the captioning score table is combined with a redrawn latency plot. The memory-growth and attention-distribution figures disappear, while two detailed benchmark-wise training-curve figures replace the earlier grouped curve.

R1.justification: The relationship to prior work changes from proposing a necessary architectural remedy for existing cross-attention approaches to arguing that standard cross-attention was underestimated under differing training pipelines. V2 adds gist-token/context-compression positioning and citations such as LXMERT and linear-transformer work, while removing several positional/context-extension references. This is a substantive repositioning, beyond citation renumbering.

T1.justification: The attention equations largely match after renaming, including v1 Equation 3 and v2 Equation 4. Formal efficiency content changes: v1's theoretical attention-memory expressions in Table 1 and Figure 3 are replaced by per-variant KV-cache counts in v2 Table 1. Neither version contains substantive theorem or proof developments.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves an important comparison confound: v1 Table 2 uses 0.3T training tokens for CASA versus 0.1T for insertion, with different training resolutions; v2 uses 0.13T and the same maximum resolution for both. The resulting controlled comparisons support a more measured conclusion about vanilla cross-attention and are complemented by explicit video-history controls. Some profiling detail is lost, and appendix inconsistencies remain, including old resolution values in Section B.2, but the improved validity of the central comparison constitutes a substantial overall gain.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CASA research, with shared backbones, datasets, experiments, and retained results despite substantial reframing. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v2 reports original cross-attention training and adaptation results, architectural comparisons, video evaluations, efficiency measurements, and training curves, alongside retained original results.

before.justification: v1 reports original Helium-based training, Qwen2.5-VL adaptation, ablations, efficiency measurements, and video-captioning experiments in the main text and appendices.

results.title: CASA: Cross-Attention over Self-Attention for Efficient Vision-Language Fusion

C1.justification: Both versions claim that reasoning improves small VLMs' grounding efficiency, narrows the gap with larger models, and generalizes to amodal grounding. The headline 91.4 versus 90.5 comparison and 5.9× speedup remain. The revised title and token-cost framing change emphasis without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 newly argues that gains chiefly arise from reasoning and invokes commercial models' lower grounding scores against a distillation explanation in Section 5.3. It adds interpretations concerning hard-case recovery, model-size-dependent reasoning benefits, and practical occlusion handling. These refine the retained mechanism and applicability arguments rather than replace them.

D1.justification: V3 clarifies separate training for vanilla and amodal tasks and documents the JSON-schema ablation control. Its title page removes 'coming soon' and adds a model-access link. Conversely, data-curation passages replace GPT-4 identification with an unnamed proprietary VLM, and Section 5.2 drops the explicit latency-times-GPU-count definition. Existing hyperparameters, dataset sizes, hardware, and prompt templates remain.

E1.justification: The RefCOCO-family benchmarks and COCO-Amodal/TAO-Amodal data coverage remain. V3 adds qualitative amodal-grounding demonstrations on driving images and a DROID robotics example in Figure 4. This extends evaluated environments modestly without establishing new quantitative driving or manipulation benchmarks.

E2.justification: V3 adds SFT-only and reasoning-disabled comparison variants, plus Gemini-3-Pro in the complex-prompt, vanilla, and amodal comparisons. Conversely, its amodal table omits v1's InternVL-3-38B, Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct, Qwen3-VL-32B-Thinking, and Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct entries. The new component controls substantially expand the comparison methods beyond the original baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: V3 adds substantial control and diagnostic protocols: evaluating SFT-stage checkpoints, suppressing intermediate reasoning through a JSON schema, and tracking baseline failures using pre/post IoU bins. Failure attribution expands from GPT-4 alone to three model judges. These additions broaden the evaluation design; the retained benchmark splits, training budgets, and standard inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Unlike v1, v3 includes SFT/RL stage ablations, reasoning-suppression ablations across six models, and a hard-case recovery analysis in Appendices E–G. Appendix H expands failure analysis across judges and categories, while Figure 4 adds application case studies. The older Qwen qualitative examples are relocated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Dataset spread summaries and RL rollout sample counts are retained. The additional model judges extend the analysis design but are not presented as statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained headline scores are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results in Tables 9–12, including Qwen3-VL-8B EGM accuracy of 88.6 without reasoning versus 91.4 with it, and recovery of 3,030/6,082 hard cases. Gemini-3-Pro achieves 85.2 vanilla, 71.9 amodal, and 57.3 complex-subset accuracy. Some amodal results disappear. Section 5.3 also corrects gains to match retained tables, such as Qwen 2B's +5.5 becoming +6.0.

M1.justification: The reasoning-data pipeline, learnability-based RL sampling, SFT followed by GRPO, and reward remain unchanged. Renaming negative/positive samples to learnable/easy samples preserves the selection rules. Reasoning suppression is introduced as an experimental control, not a modification of the proposed EGM method.

P1.justification: The title, introductory framing, and RL-selection explanation are revised, including learnable/easy sample terminology. Existing Qwen qualitative discussion moves from Appendix C into new Section 5.6. Much of the earlier prose and section sequence is retained; the added scientific analyses account for much of the expansion.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of displays. V3 reorganizes the failure-subset and amodal tables, adds an RL-selection panel to Figure 3, introduces application demonstrations and analysis tables, and moves the existing Qwen qualitative figure into the main text.

R1.justification: V3 adds DROID and TARGO references supporting robotics examples and removes several background citations, including the original Qwen report and pix2gestalt. The overall positioning within grounding, amodal perception, and reasoning research remains, including the claim to first study amodal grounding in VLMs.

T1.justification: The grounding-success definition, learnability criterion, GRPO objective, advantage calculation, and reward equations remain substantively unchanged. Sample-set renaming is mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs; the new hard-sample bins concern empirical evaluation.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked direct component ablations despite attributing its gains to reasoning-based training. V3's Tables 9–10 supply training-stage and reasoning-suppression controls, while Tables 11–12 strengthen hard-case and failure-diagnosis evidence. These substantially improve assessment of the central mechanism without changing headline scores. Some amodal comparisons and generator-specific details are lost, and the controls do not fully establish the argument against distillation, but the added empirical scrutiny addresses an important evidential gap and provides a substantial net improvement.

A1.justification: Despite the changed title and layout, both PDFs describe the same EGM work, with matching methods and retained experiments. All 22 pages of v1 and 33 pages of v3, including Appendices A–D and A–H respectively, support comparison through readable text, equations, tables, and figures.

after.justification: V3 retains original grounding and efficiency results and adds component ablations, hard-sample analysis, additional model comparisons, and application demonstrations.

before.justification: V1 reports original EGM grounding experiments, failure-case analyses, qualitative predictions, and latency measurements, including Tables 1, 3–4 and Figure 4.

results.title: EGM: Efficient Visual Grounding Language Models

C1.justification: The panoramic-interface, ScanRefer/Nr3D performance and generalization claims remain. v2's introduction explicitly extends the applicability claim to casually captured RGB frames with off-the-shelf reconstruction. Its conclusion also omits v1's explicit open-vocabulary characterization.

C2.justification: v1's limitations paragraph mainly lists future tasks; v2 explicitly discusses reconstruction dependence, noise sensitivity and slower VLM inference. Added analyses explain ambiguous-reference, occlusion and partial-object failures, interpret backbone tradeoffs, and qualify the adapter design by finding exact mid/late placement noncritical (Appendices C–E).

D1.justification: v2 newly documents ground-truth initialization of the existing 3DGS variant, automatic reconstruction and checkpoint reuse, detailed QA supervision, smartphone capture specifications, 30K reconstruction steps, and stage-level CPU/GPU memory and timing. These substantially expand deployment and reproducibility information. The five-epoch training budget was already disclosed in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds grounding under fully automated RGB-only reconstruction without ground-truth meshes or camera trajectories, plus a new self-captured living-room demonstration (Appendices C.1 and D.2). These substantially extend tested input conditions beyond the benchmark reconstructions in v1; the principal named benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: New Table 2 compares against ZSVG3D, SeeGround and VLM-Grounder in zero-shot Nr3D evaluation. Appendix D.1 adds LLaVA-3D to the resource comparison. Conversely, TSP3D is removed from Table 1. These change actual comparator participation, beyond citation or naming edits.

E3.justification: v2 restricts the representation comparison to 92 of 141 validation scenes, requiring at least 300 COLMAP-registered images, and evaluates automatic reconstructions with the existing 3DGS checkpoint. It also introduces zero-shot, smaller-backbone and linear-probe protocols. The text-variant table's metric changes from Acc@0.25 to Top-1, with unchanged values; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an all-feature control without EMD, inference-time geometry masking, adapter-layer ablations and linear probes, scene-size/category/elevation analyses, backbone scalability tests and explicit failure cases. Existing camera-placement, initialization, convergence and rotation analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 introduces a linear fit and correlation reporting for floor area versus camera count (r=0.80), adding a statistical estimation procedure absent from v1. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained headline scores are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results, including 53.2 zero-shot Nr3D accuracy and 52.1 ScanRefer accuracy with Qwen2.5-VL-7B. The representation comparison replaces v1's ScanRefer 3DGS/mesh scores of 59.3/61.0 with 60.8/61.6 on the restricted subset and adds automatic 3DGS at 55.1; these are not same-setting gains. Nr3D/Sr3D representation results are removed, while new diagnostic, resource and qualitative outcomes are added.

M1.justification: The stated geometric adapter band changes from [L/3,2L/3] to [L/3,2L/3), removing the shared endpoint with the semantic band (v1 Section 3.3; v2 Section 3.2). The core pipeline and objectives remain intact. Axis-based geometric QA was already documented in v1 Appendix A.4.

P1.justification: Substantial passages in the introduction, related work and method are rewritten. Panorama construction and adapters are merged into one subsection, benchmark discussion is consolidated, pinhole comparisons move under ablations, and the appendix is reorganized around analyses and deployment. Terminology and affiliations also change.
