P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout, replaces the introductory overview, redraws pipeline and adapter diagrams, and adds numerous diagnostic and deployment displays. Two earlier appendix examples reappear in the introductory figure. The representation table is restructured, and existing mesh/3DGS images gain explanatory annotations.

R1.justification: v2 adds SpatialRGPT, COLMAP and visual-representation analysis citations while pruning works including SAT, LAR, ScanReason and TSP3D. Related work more explicitly contrasts curated 3D inputs, limited viewing coverage and specialized 3D tokens with PanoGrounder, while retaining the original central research positioning.

T1.justification: The camera-scoring, cross-view consistency, aggregation and weighted digit-EMD mathematics are retained. v2 explicitly writes the standard cross-entropy formula and clarifies notation, without adding a substantive derivation, theoretical assumption, theorem or proof.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for practical applicability and the contribution beyond a large backbone: it adds automatic reconstruction tests, a real capture demonstration, resource accounting, smaller-backbone comparisons and diagnostic controls. Concrete limitations and failure cases also improve transparency. The reconstruction comparison becomes narrower, excluding 49 validation scenes and dropping Nr3D/Sr3D representation results, while LIFT-GS retains its original evaluation setting. These limits constrain that comparison, but the added validation addresses important gaps in v1 and yields a substantial net improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PanoGrounder. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds zero-shot comparisons, reconstruction and deployment experiments, backbone evaluations and diagnostic analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding experiments, cross-dataset and text generalization results, ablations, qualitative analyses and runtime measurements.

results.title: PanoGrounder: Bridging 2D and 3D with Panoramic Scene Representations for VLM-based 3D Visual Grounding

C1.justification: The central task, counterfactual benchmark and robustness–reading trade-off claims remain. However, v2 narrows RIO-RT from a novel defense acquiring a new capability to a minimal reference baseline, explicitly making benchmarking the primary contribution and claiming largely preserved reading performance.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies causal and applicability claims: vision-only defenses are no longer described as inherently incompatible with reading, and cross-dataset transfer is described more cautiously. Limitations now include incomplete typography/threat-model coverage and the fixed SFT recipe and budget. SceneTAP results receive a new interpretation as transfer beyond training-time overlays.

D1.justification: v2 specifies AdamW and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and documents SceneTAP masks, fallbacks, components and computational costs. Conversely, it removes some exact OCR-matching details, the smallest-index QA-selection rule, the project-page pointer and the explicit code-release promise. These are documentation changes, not evidence that external resources became unavailable.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation-only SceneTAP conditions for object MC/OE and text OE, extending digital-overlay testing to scene-coherent generative insertions. The underlying TextVQA/Open Images coverage and external Typo-D, AI2D, ChartQA, DocVQA and InfoVQA evaluations were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Direct comparisons against RIO-RT retain the original models, CoT and IT-RT on the same six backbones. v2 Table 5 separately evaluates additional unmodified LVLMs for capability and scaling; it does not introduce another competing defense into the RIO-RT comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the stated placement grid from 7×7 to 11×11 and overlap-resampling limit from 100 to 200. New protocols include the four-stratum human audit and frontier/scaling evaluations averaging hard-overlay and SceneTAP scores. Appendix B also revises scoring descriptions. These documented changes do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a 400-sample audit of answerability and distractor validity, tests transfer from overlay-only training to unseen SceneTAP attacks, and analyzes model scaling. New qualitative SceneTAP cases accompany these tests. Existing LoRA-placement, attention, external-dataset and training-data-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: The new audit introduces three-annotator reliability reporting, including raw agreement of 90.0–94.3% and Gwet’s AC1 of 0.89–0.94. Neither version supplies repeated-training-run uncertainty or confidence intervals for model performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds SceneTAP, audit and frontier/scaling results. Table 5 reports GPT-5.4 object accuracy of 96.4 clean versus 74.3 attacked, and Gemini-2.5-Pro at 96.1 versus 77.7. Retained entries also change, such as original LLaVA-1.5-7B object-clean accuracy from 93.5 to 93.7. Expanded attack averages are not directly comparable with v1’s overlay-only averages.

M1.justification: RIO-RT retains its balanced SFT/LoRA procedure. Benchmark construction adds an adapted SceneTAP insertion branch with OCR-preserving masks and placement fallbacks. Appendix A.2 also revises the described negative-label selection through CLIP-filtered exclusions, ancestor exclusion and a training-vocabulary restriction.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, benchmark explanations and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten around relevant scene text versus inserted distractors. Appendix descriptions are substantially condensed and reorganized, alongside new audit and frontier-evaluation sections. This exceeds terminology or numbering changes.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a single-column layout, merges v1 Figures 1–2, expands result tables with SceneTAP columns, and adds audit/frontier tables and a SceneTAP qualitative figure. Appendix Figures 6–11 gain SceneTAP panels and several corrected question labels. Retained attention and data-size plots are largely redisplayed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gwet’s reliability reference and removes the general adversarial-attack references by Brown, Goodfellow and Madry. Most related work remains, including the previously cited SceneTAP. Positioning becomes more restrained, presenting RIO-RT as a complementary baseline rather than a fundamentally novel alternative to prior defenses.

T1.justification: Appendix B replaces v1’s leave-one-annotator-out TextVQA formula with min(matching answers/3, 1), which is mathematically different for partial agreement. The explicit multi-label CLIP-M definition is also omitted in favor of a single-ground-truth formulation. The R-CLIP-M subtraction principle remains; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

improvement.justification: The 400-sample human audit directly addresses v1’s lack of empirical validation for automated benchmark construction, while unseen SceneTAP tests strengthen evidence beyond digital overlays. Frontier evaluations and more restrained claims further improve relevance and calibration. These substantial gains outweigh reporting regressions: metric descriptions lose precision, and Table 6 retains 34,826 evaluation samples although its expanded rows sum to 44,324, weakening reproducibility.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RIO-VQA, RIO-Bench and RIO-RT work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and added experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds SceneTAP evaluations, a human audit, and modern/frontier-model experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original LVLM evaluations, defense comparisons, LoRA ablations, attention analyses and cross-dataset generalization results, including Appendix F.

results.title: Read or Ignore? A Unified Benchmark for Typographic-Attack Robustness and Text Recognition in Vision-Language Models

C1.justification: Both versions claim textbook-grounded hierarchical and DDx supervision, SFT followed by hierarchical RL, superior diagnostic performance, and the importance of SFT initialization. The revised title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain these central contributions.

C2.justification: The new discussion explicitly distinguishes answer accuracy from reasoning faithfulness, acknowledges coupling between training knowledge and taxonomy-generated evaluation options, and limits conclusions about other backbones and clinical deployment. Appendices G and I additionally discuss speculative reasoning, excessive reliance on rules, and population sensitivity. These substantially qualify v1's largely affirmative interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the textbook source and documents clustering, image-text pairing, gpt-4.1-mini extraction and prompts, graph statistics, 2,020 trajectories, and pairing settings. It expands extraction and evaluation details and reports released code, weights, and reasoning annotations with copyright restrictions. Conversely, v1's OOD subset-count table is removed. These are primarily documentation and access changes, not established procedural revisions.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation across Fitzpatrick skin types using a Fitzpatrick-17k subset (Appendix I), which v1 excluded from OOD testing. The six RL datasets, five main OOD benchmarks, and existing diagnostic tasks remain represented.

E2.justification: Tables 4–5 add an evaluated 'RL with standard reward' comparison variant using a binary reward. The external VLM baseline membership remains unchanged; newly cited research does not introduce additional evaluated external baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the stated representative checkpoint from 1,000 to 1,500 RL steps, aligning the text with retained table results without establishing a rerun. The added reward ablation introduces a binary-reward control. Existing splits, principal metrics, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct test of the granularity reward (Tables 4–5), answer-extraction validity analysis (Table 6), and skin-type analysis (Table 8). Qualitative evidence expands from four cases to five open-ended and five closed-ended cases, including a Skin-R1 failure. These substantially broaden mechanism testing and examination of evaluation reliability and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Greedy evaluation is retained. The new extraction percentages and subgroup scores are additional outcomes, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All retained numerical entries in Tables 2–5 match. V2 substantially extends the findings with standard-reward results, including OOD average 0.6386 versus Skin-R1's retained 0.7171, extraction-validity percentages, skin-type scores, and additional case outcomes. It removes v1's reported 800-step RL-without-SFT results of 0.5120 accuracy and 0.3664 F1. These are added and removed findings, not improved headline performance.

M1.justification: The textbook-to-SFT-to-GRPO pipeline and Algorithms 1–4 are retained; most additions document construction details. However, v1 Appendix A explicitly mentions SkinCon/Fitzpatrick concept-alignment training, whereas v2 removes this statement and associated notation. The PDFs do not clarify whether training changed or an inconsistent earlier description was corrected.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting affects the abstract, introduction, related work, methods, and experimental narrative. V2 adds overview and key-findings blocks, retitles the paper, replaces the conclusion with Summary and Discussion, and reorganizes the appendices into separate extraction, construction, examples, implementation, and analysis sections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a narrower conference layout, restyles tables, relocates and rescales figures, and reformats cases with monospaced text and diagnostic color annotations. Dataset-summary and OOD-distribution tables disappear; extraction-validity and skin-type tables and a reward illustration are added. The notation table is also revised.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Fitzpatrick's Dermatology, Skinflow, and a 2026 dermatology foundation-model paper, and explicitly credits the extraction pipeline to the already-cited Kim et al. work. PPO and DPO references disappear with their comparison paragraph. The broader positioning against existing medical VLM approaches remains stable.

T1.justification: V1 Equation (7) incorrectly drops the 0.75 factor in its final equality; v2 Equation (8) restores it. The explicit zero reward for off-path predictions agrees with v1 Appendix A. This is a localized mathematical correction; the SFT and GRPO objectives remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V1 inadequately documented creation of its central supervision resource and lacked a direct control for the hierarchical reward. V2 substantially improves reproducibility through Appendices B–C and J, tests that reward in Tables 4–5, and adds explicit limitations and failure evidence. These strengthen the paper despite unchanged headline scores. The unresolved concept-alignment history, missing uncertainty estimates, and loss of OOD sample counts remain weaknesses.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Skin-R1. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and appendix expansion.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds a reward ablation, answer-extraction validity results, skin-type evaluation, and additional qualitative cases.

before.justification: V1 reports original diagnostic evaluations, training-stage ablations, training curves, targeted DDx and hierarchical tests, and qualitative cases.

results.title: Skin-R1: Clinical Knowledge-Guided Dermatological Diagnosis Using Vision-Language Models

C1.justification: v2 emphasizes being the first multi-step spatial-reasoning benchmark and exploratory transfer to image generation. v4 recasts the contribution around Elementary and Planning sets, explicit plans through eight steps and multi-turn generation. Its abstract replaces the approximate half-accuracy ceiling with a remaining human gap and new claims of planning collapse, including zero accuracy for three-step generation.

C2.justification: v4 identifies incorrect step selection as a failure preceding ordering and discusses temporal and physical consistency requirements for generation. Appendix A attributes some human Height errors to insufficient attention; Appendix E argues that automatic judging reliably detects obvious failures but struggles with precise spatial judgments. v2's CoT and Qwen2.5-VL robustness interpretations are removed.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D newly provide eleven Elementary-task prompts, detailed task-specific scoring rubrics, annotator calibration and averaging procedures, and explanations of automatic versus human ground-truth construction. v4 also supplies identifiers for its new image-generation models. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation; the original project, code and dataset links remain.

E1.justification: The original 11 tasks become the Elementary set. v4 adds planning that requires selecting and ordering correct states among distractors, plus generating complete intermediate trajectories over multiple turns. These introduce distinct task requirements. v2's Next-k-Step scenario, selecting a state after adding specified pieces, is removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands from 20 to 29 models, adding GPT-5, GPT-o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen3-VL/InternVL3/3.5 variants. Table 2 replaces five of six model comparators. The generation table adds GPT-5 and Nano Banana Pro and removes the numerical GPT-4o△ column, although that model's examples remain as GPT-4o* in the appendix. Planning generation also evaluates Nano Banana 2.

E3.justification: New planning VQA uses 20 cases per horizon, k correct and k distractor options, exact-match/set-match/overlap scoring and five human experts. Generation introduces topology-expanded valid trajectories, MSE matching and binary trajectory scoring. These differ substantially from v2's four-option Next-k-Step protocol with/without CoT. The generation sample count is inconsistent: 50 total cases versus 10 cases for each of four horizons.

E4.justification: v2's Next-k-Step/CoT ablation and its robustness findings are removed. v4 adds planning-error decomposition through exact versus set matching, human Height-error cases and an attention recheck, and human-versus-LLM judging analyses (Appendices A and E). Additional trajectory and single-turn generation cases expand the failure analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals or error bars. The random-guessing significance thresholds and cross-benchmark Pearson coefficients/p-values are retained. The new judge-agreement correlations and MAE/MSE values are evaluation results, without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Shared Table 1 scores remain unchanged, including GPT-4o's 57.7%; v4 adds GPT-5 at 72.0% overall and 71.8% on Lite against humans' retained 93.6%. New planning results show GPT-5 exact match declining from 90% at k=1 to 0% at k=8, and all tested generators scoring zero at k=3–5. Next-k-Step/CoT results disappear, while appendix judge-agreement results are added.

M1.justification: Section 3.2.2 adds a turn-by-turn generation procedure in which each intermediate image is conditioned on previously generated states, extending v2's single-output generation setup. This is a limited inference-procedure adaptation; no new architecture, learned component or training objective is introduced, and the original curation pipeline remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten. Dataset definitions and experiments are reorganized around separate Elementary and Planning sets. The original image-generation evaluation moves into the discussion as an analysis of elementary generation failures, while dedicated appendix sections organize prompts, scoring guidance and case studies.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains a planning example; the original Figure 2 is split, with a rearranged pipeline and the statistics chart moved to Appendix B. Comparison tables expand and reorder, the CoT table disappears, and new planning curves, trajectory panels, Height-error examples and judge-agreement tables are introduced. Generation grids are updated and expanded.

R1.justification: v4 replaces much of v2's reasoning-enhancement discussion with detailed positioning against spatial and planning benchmarks, including PhyBlock, ActPlan-1K, OrigamiSpace and GamiBench. It adds LEGO-related cognitive studies and newer-model references, and shifts novelty positioning toward challenging explicit planning and multi-turn generation.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical results, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations. The added sequence notation, assembly-validity conditions and standard set-match/overlap scoring descriptions specify empirical tasks and protocols rather than introduce new mathematical theory.

improvement.justification: The new controlled planning tasks, human reference results and error decomposition substantially strengthen evidence for the central multi-step reasoning claims beyond v2's narrower tests. Elementary-task prompts, explicit scoring rubrics and evidence about automated judging also improve reproducibility and interpretation. These gains outweigh the loss of the CoT ablation and the unresolved generation sample-count inconsistency, which still weakens that experiment's reporting.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LEGO-Puzzles and retain matching original tasks and results. Text, tables and figures support comparison throughout. v2 ends with references and has no appendix; v4 includes readable Appendices A–G.

after.justification: v4 reports evaluations of 29 MLLMs, human comparisons, new planning experiments and image-generation results. Appendix E additionally reports original comparisons between GPT-4o judging and human ratings.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 20 MLLMs, human comparisons, image-generation experiments, Next-k-Step/CoT experiments and cross-benchmark correlations in Tables 1–5.

results.title: LEGO-Puzzles: How Good Are MLLMs at Multi-Step Spatial Reasoning?

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: spatially grounded hierarchical concepts, improved naming, and interpretable foundation-model applications beyond classification with competitive downstream performance. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The added analyses explain guided pooling's importance, sparsity/locality/consistency tradeoffs, and applicability to a larger backbone. Figure C7 adds specific naming-failure interpretations, including lexical gaps and spurious correlations. Section C.8 qualifies steering effectiveness through category-dependent failures. The main conclusion and existing limitations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the relationship judge's full prompt, composite-image construction and filtering details, identifies the SigLIP-2 variant, and explicitly documents ImageNet-only SAE training for Appendix B.8. It also adds an interactive-visualization address. Existing core training hyperparameters and captioning hardware/time disclosures are retained.

E1.justification: The datasets, domains, and underlying classification, segmentation, concept-assessment, and caption-steering tasks are retained. SigLIP-2 changes the model configuration; the systematic COCO steering and hierarchy-direction evaluations add protocols and analyses within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure C15 introduces a CLIP target-word steering baseline against CFM's concept steering; v2 supplied qualitative steering examples without this comparison. The comparator sets in the retained main classification, concept-quality, captioning, and segmentation experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include judging 1,000 hierarchy pairs using top-five examples and consistency/directionality filtering, and testing caption deletion with 80 samples per COCO category using text matching and an LLM judge. Appendix B.8 adds a 400M-parameter SigLIP-2 configuration and controlled ImageNet-trained architecture variants. These are added experimental settings, not demonstrated reruns of the retained headline experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's dictionary-size and reconstruction/sparsity analyses, v3 tests guided-pooling removal, alternative SAE objectives, sparsity effects on downstream performance and interpretability, and backbone scaling. It also adds hierarchy-direction validation and quantitative category-wise steering analysis. Table 2 extends the existing dictionary-size analysis with C2 scores.

E5.justification: The new relationship-judge prompt requests a confidence rating from 1 to 5, and Figure A6 displays an example rating. This adds limited per-judgment confidence reporting, rather than statistical uncertainty for aggregate accuracy. The existing Wilcoxon test is retained; no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Figure 3 changes CFM's C2 score from 0.405 to 0.465, and Figure C9 changes the plotted distributions. New results include 86.2% ImageNet accuracy for CFM with SigLIP-2, hierarchy-direction accuracy of 300/376 filtered pairs, and steering deletion rates of 25.9% versus 21.3% by LLM judging and 28.2% versus 23.2% by text matching. The per-dataset 4k/16k segmentation results from v2 Table B1 are omitted when condensed into v3 Table 2.

M1.justification: The core CFM pipeline is retained, but the stated naming procedure changes in Eq. (B.8): alpha now scales the combined child and parent vectors, whereas v2 applied it only to the child vector. The accompanying explanation changes accordingly. This establishes a limited procedural revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 4.3 and Appendix A.3, expands B.8 and C.8, and makes localized grammar, terminology, caption, and cross-reference corrections. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation expands substantially: v2 Tables B1/B2 are condensed into main-text Table 2, new backbone and architecture tables are added, and new figures present the relationship-judge prompt/example and quantitative steering. Figure C9 is enlarged and redrawn with mean markers. Existing qualitative examples are retained, including the steering figure renumbered C16.

R1.justification: The same 86 reference entries and substantive research positioning are retained. Corrections to existing CLIP-DINOiser and COCO-Object citations do not introduce new cited works or redefine the relationship to prior research.

T1.justification: Equation (2) changes the numerator's activation weight from A_ip to A_jp, making it consistent with the stated conditional-probability definition. Equations (3) and (4) replace argmin with argmax, matching the maximum-similarity rule; Eq. (3) also removes the bias from the prior-method expression. These are substantive mathematical corrections, without new theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: v3 materially strengthens validation of the central design and steering claims. Controlled architecture ablations address questions left open by v2's narrower analyses, and quantitative steering supplies a baseline comparison beyond selected examples. Mathematical corrections also improve internal consistency. These gains outweigh the loss of detailed dictionary-size segmentation scores and the new steering text's reversal of the solid/hatched legend mapping. The hierarchy-direction result remains conditional on 376 of 1,000 sampled pairs, limiting its generality.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CFM research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

after.justification: v3 reports original human-study and downstream-task results, together with architecture ablations, backbone-scaling experiments, hierarchy-direction evaluation, and quantitative caption steering.

before.justification: v2 reports original concept-quality measurements, a human study, classification, captioning, segmentation, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

results.title: CFM: Language-aligned Concept Foundation Model for Vision

C1.justification: The three principal contributions and the first-reference-based-VLM claim remain. v2 nevertheless removes v1's explicit introductory suggestion of even unsupervised deployment, retaining a more limited-supervision framing.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning spatial versus semantic reference cues, failures under large reference mismatch, and why medical segmentation baselines fail to select targets. It removes v1's qualification that specialized nnU-Net achieves better segmentation. Its new claim that LISA-SFT and SegZero-SFT degrade sharply on OOD data is not consistently supported by Table 3's scores across different datasets.

D1.justification: Appendices B and C substantially expand implementation documentation: DINOv2 ViT-S/14 preprocessing, FAISS retrieval with K=5, augmentation, evaluation-set sizes, JSONL conversation structure, QLoRA configuration, gradient accumulation, context length, and trainable components. These are primarily disclosures rather than established procedural changes. Reproducibility remains limited by conflicting dropout/epoch descriptions and missing detailed RL and runtime information despite the main-text pointer.

E1.justification: The benchmark datasets and modalities are retained; AMOS2022-MRI, CT-Liver, and CT-Lung already appeared in v1's Table 1. v2 adds a spatially shuffled-reference test scenario and an interactive annotation-refinement task, without establishing a new benchmark dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds HuatuoGPT-Vision, Lingshu, MedRegA, BiRD, and MedPLIB. Table 3 adds MedSAM2-Memory, MedSAM2-Memory-Ref-SFT, LISA-SFT, and SegZero-SFT alongside retained SAM2 baselines. New Table 5 also evaluates SAM2 with ground-truth boxes. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The hyperparameter table changes the reported epoch count from 3 to 5; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Added evaluations introduce ground-truth-box controls, shuffled references, LPIPS similarity bins, and a one-annotator study measuring time and clicks for 30 images containing 153 targets. Existing benchmark metrics and Table 1 training schedules remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained labeling-accuracy initialization ablation, v2 adds segmentation-metric ablations of VLM initialization/RL, oracle box prompting, and shuffled reference layouts in Table 5. Table S2 examines sensitivity to reference similarity, Figures S5–S6 show localization and segmentation failures, and Appendix C.6 investigates annotation effort.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results retain point-estimate reporting; the annotation study's participant and image counts describe its evaluation sample.

E6.justification: Retained table entries remain numerically unchanged, but v2 adds substantial comparator, ablation, sensitivity, and annotation-cost results. For example, Table 5 reports RAOS Dice of 0.2088 with shuffled references versus 0.7151 for full RAU; Appendix C.6 reports 24.9 minutes versus nearly 250 for MedSAM2-Memory-Ref-SFT. Section 3.2 also revises its quoted RAOS comparison from 64.11% versus 78.16% to 74.68% versus 78.16%, using the retained RL-VQA baseline.

M1.justification: The Qwen/GRPO, global box-matching, and SAM2 architecture remains. However, v2's new experimental description and Appendix C.3 specify reference-image bounding boxes, conflicting with the target-image outputs described in v1 and retained in v2's Section 3.2. The PDFs do not resolve whether this reflects a procedure change or inconsistent documentation.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively rewritten, Section 3 gains a new explanatory roadmap, and method subsections separate methods, settings, and results. The conclusion is condensed, while the appendix is reorganized into datasets and task-specific experimental sections. These changes extend beyond accommodating new results.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography and page layout, expands Table 1, transposes and expands Table 3, and adds Table 5, Table S2, and failure-case Figures S5–S6. Figure 2 is reworked. Earlier Figures A1–A4 are retained as S3, S4, S1, and S2, respectively, with relocation and caption/layout edits rather than new qualitative evidence.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially reframes RAU against non-VLM clinical pipelines and medical VLM grounding, explicitly separating the reference-conditioned task from the algorithmic contribution. New medical-model, segmentation, retrieval, and clinical references broaden the positioning. The GLIP and SEEM citations also change from unrelated works in v1 to different grounding/segmentation papers.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), including the VQA formulation, rewards, optimal-transport assignment, and memory attention, retain their mathematical substance. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new empirical analyses introduce no substantive mathematical development.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis of RAU: broader medical-VLM and segmentation comparisons address v1's narrow comparator coverage, while shuffled-reference controls and reference-quality analyses directly examine the central spatial-reasoning claim and its failure boundaries. Expanded implementation documentation also improves assessability. These gains outweigh the unresolved output/training inconsistencies, removal of the nnU-Net qualification, and unsupported blanket interpretation of OOD baseline deterioration.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAU. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting and supplementary-material reorganization.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, segmentation and reference-quality analyses, failure cases, and an annotation-cost study.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA, bounding-box labeling, segmentation, and initialization-ablation results in Tables 1–4, with qualitative examples in the appendix.

results.title: RAU: Reference-based Anatomical Understanding with Vision-Language Models

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about automated task-wise discovery, semantic exploration, performance and efficiency, and model-specific prompting. The added experiments provide further support without redefining these main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the toolbox ablation as evidence that external models are not the main source of BlindTest gains, while acknowledging task-specific benefits. It also acknowledges the Claude CircledLetter exception, explicitly limits split-stability conclusions to CircledLetter, and explains how initially weaker search nodes can support useful refinements.

D1.justification: Appendix C specifies the permitted and excluded tool functions and explains construction of the additional development splits and held-out test set. The original hyperparameters, tool descriptions, Appendix A prompts, and Appendix B development indices remain unchanged. No new code or data access instructions are supplied.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four BlindTest tasks and five BLINK tasks described in Section 4.1 and Appendix B. The added backbone, toolbox, and split experiments reuse this coverage without introducing different data populations or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table A1 adds Basic-tool SEVEX as an internal comparison variant against full-tool SEVEX and Naive. The existing Naive, SketchPad, SketchPad+APE, and search-component comparisons remain; Table 5 reuses the Naive and SketchPad comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 expands evaluation beyond v1's single-task cross-backbone transfer experiment with full-discovery comparisons across four BlindTest tasks using GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 4.0. It also introduces a restricted-tool control and two additional 30-image CircledLetter development splits, excluding their union from testing. These substantially extend the evaluation design while retaining the original metrics and main search settings.

E4.justification: The original component ablations and qualitative analyses are retained. New Appendix C tests whether gains depend on external pretrained tools, examines sensitivity to development-set selection, and presents a per-trial search trace. These add substantive evidence about attribution, robustness, and search behavior.

E5.justification: v1 already reports Figure 5 averages over five independent runs. v2 additionally specifies five runs per new development split and reports means with within-split standard deviations in Table A2. This adds explicit variability reporting for one study without revising the original run counts.

E6.justification: Original Tables 2–4 retain their values. Table 5 adds backbone/task results, including SEVEX averages of 62.4% for GPT-4o and 75.2% for Claude, while reusing Gemini and some LineIntersections entries. Table A1 adds a 73.3% basic-tool average versus 72.4% with full tools. Table A2 reports test accuracies of 88.00 ± 4.30% and 85.98 ± 3.86% under the new split protocol. These are additional results, not revised same-setting performance gains.

M1.justification: The abstract-idea search tree, novelty-guided UCT, implementation loop, semantic backpropagation, expansion rules, and Appendix A prompts are unchanged. The restricted-tool variant is an experimental control; the proposed default procedure remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 condenses Section 2.1, corrects grammar and terminology, and consistently identifies the CircledLetter ablation. It inserts a backbone subsection and an additional-analyses appendix, moves the existing Discussions appendix from C to D, and adds contact information and acknowledgements. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, Tables A1–A2, and Figure A1 using the established presentation style. Existing displays are retained, with localized resizing and relocation, corrected captions and the Figure 5 task label, and changes to reference-link coloring. The original figures and tables are not substantially redesigned.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 softens the research-gap description from lacking research to being underexplored and replaces the claim of the first agent-driven system with an agent-driven system. The same 25 cited works remain; bibliography corrections do not add related research.

T1.justification: The search-tree definitions and priority equations (1)–(2) are unchanged. The added explanation of search behavior introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation by extending the main multi-task comparisons beyond Gemini and adding a direct control for external-tool dependence, addressing important gaps in v1's evidence for generality and attribution. Table A2 adds repeated-run variability and development-split robustness evidence with an explicit CircledLetter-only limitation. These gains improve support for the central method while preserving the original experiments and technical material.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEVEX, with matching methods, benchmarks, and original experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds backbone comparisons, restricted-tool experiments, development-split sensitivity results, and a search trace.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, inference and exploration costs, component ablations, and cross-backbone prompt-transfer experiments in Tables 2–4 and Figure 5.
